## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Scripted Gameplay Videos (Multi-Scene Capture)

In a scripted video capture we create a level, play it for x seconds, then capture y seconds, pause the video capture. Create a new level, play it for x seconds, capture y seconds. There should be a fade to black and a fade from black lasting 0.25 seconds between each scene. There are an arbitrary number of scenes.

## Problem statement

The current capture system produces a **single continuous video** per invocation — either one full demo run with a tail (`npm run capture`) or a fixed-length scripted clip (`--duration`). There is no way to compile several distinct gameplay segments into one video with transitions. This feature adds **multi-scene** capture: sequence several gameplay scenes, play each for a configured duration, capture each for a configured duration, and stitch them into one video with 0.25 s fade-to-black / fade-from-black transitions between scenes.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can define a sequence of scenes in a config file and capture each one with play/capture durations and fade transitions, producing a single compiled video showing multiple gameplay segments for demo / showcase / marketing purposes.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants showcase videos that demonstrate several distinct gameplay elements (player control, weapons, power-ups, enemy archetypes, boss phases) in one compiled video, rather than multiple separate recordings.
- **Secondary — prospective players / viewers.** The audience of the showcase: they should see a smooth, non-jarring sequence of varied gameplay in a single clip.

**Example user stories:**

- As the maintainer, I can write a JSON scene list of gym scenes with per-scene play/capture timings and record them all in one command, so I get a single showcase video.
- As a viewer, I see a clean fade-to-black then fade-from-black between segments, so the compiled video reads as one coherent piece rather than a jarring cut.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Scene-list config.** A JSON config file specifies an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes; each entry carries a `target` (gym scene key), a `playMs` duration, a `captureMs` duration, and an optional `label`. The file is parsed and validated **before** any server/browser boots, failing fast with an actionable, non-zero-exit error for a missing/unreadable/malformed file, an unknown or unsupported `target`, an empty scene list, or a non-positive/non-numeric `playMs`/`captureMs` (mirroring the existing `--count` validation style).
- **AC2 — In-page scene director (dev-gated).** A dev-only page-side handle — e.g. `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)` — starts a discovered, non-parameterised gym scene by key **inside the already-running page** (no navigation/reload), so one continuously-running `MediaRecorder` spans every scene. It is inert in production builds (`import.meta.env.DEV` gate; `npm run check-bundle` still passes) and rejects unknown/unsupported keys (including the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`) with a clear error rather than silently doing nothing.
- **AC3 — Multi-scene capture with 0.25 s fades.** A single `MediaRecorder` captures the scenes in config order; between consecutive scenes a page-side canvas overlay fades **to** black over 0.25 s then **from** black over 0.25 s before the next scene's play window, and the fade is present in the recorded video (the recorder captures the overlay). The scene count is arbitrary (verified with at least three scenes).
- **AC4 — Single stitched output.** The command writes exactly **one** WebM (`video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus`, falling back per the existing `resolveCaptureMimeType` order) containing all scenes plus their transitions at 960×540 with the game's own SFX, and the result passes the existing non-trivial video+audio probe. The `--json` payload reports per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }` timings and the total output duration/file path.
- **AC5 — CLI entry point and documentation.** A documented entry point (e.g. `npm run capture:scenes -- --config <file>`) runs the multi-scene capture, and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the config schema, the example command and the fade behaviour. Hermetic unit tests (no browser) cover config parsing/validation, scene-plan/timing arithmetic (including the two 0.25 s fades), and the director's key-validation logic.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, and any README capture section. (`CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.)
- **AC7 — Test suite.** The full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`/skill:test`), and the build stays clean.

## Constraints

- **One recorder, one page.** Because the fades are rendered page-side, a single `MediaRecorder` runs continuously across all scenes; scene switching must therefore happen **in-page** (a page reload would end the recorder, so separate recordings + post-stitch is the wrong shape here).
- **Dev-only, shipped bundle inert.** The scene director and any `src/` plumbing are dev-gated; the production bundle and `npm run check-bundle` must be unaffected.
- **WebM only.** No `ffmpeg` is available (Playwright's bundled ffmpeg has no VP9 encoder), so the output is a single WebM — no transcoding.
- **Fades page-side (Playwright-injected canvas overlay)**, not in-engine.
- **Gym scenes are dev-only.** Option A targets dev gym scenes, not the shipped game; `GymFodderEnemies` (needs `enemyKey`) and `GymLevel` (needs a `LevelDefinition`) are parameterised and excluded from the first cut.
- Reuse existing pure capture helpers and machinery (server/browser boot, recorder plumbing, mime selection, probes) rather than duplicating them.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — single-scene capture orchestrator (Vite server, headless Chromium, record, drive bot, probe, write WebM; progress + preflight). Pure arg/mode/naming helpers are exported and unit-tested.
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — scripted bot plan + `isNonTrivialClip` / `evaluateAudioTrack` / `combineClipVerdict` predicates + the page-side audio tap.
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — run-end signal, tail/cap logic.
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — shared browser-free dev-scenario registry.
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` — pure progress/ETA formatting.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts` — hermetic tests.
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — `import.meta.glob`-based discovery of every `Gym<Name>.ts` scene (key == class name); `discoverGymScenes` / `sceneClassFromModule` are pure and unit-tested.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — dev gym index (reached from the menu's "Gym Scene Index (dev)" control); columns scenes / ENEMIES / Dev Utilities.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — dev-gated URL-selected scenarios with a page-side release handle (`window.__aiHellScenario`); the established pattern for a dev-only `window` handle gated by `import.meta.env.DEV`.
- `src/core/runEndedSignal.ts` — dev-gated page-side run-end signal/flag; the established pattern for page↔capture signalling.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — the capture documentation this feature extends.
- No fade/transition or multi-scene stitching exists in capture tooling.

## Desired change

1. A **scene-list config** (JSON, per AC1) defines an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes — each with a gym `target`, `playMs` and `captureMs`.
2. A dev-gated **in-page scene director** (`window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)`) switches scenes inside the running page, so one `MediaRecorder` spans every scene.
3. Between scenes, a **page-side canvas overlay** renders a 0.25 s fade-to-black then a 0.25 s fade-from-black, captured by the running recorder.
4. The final output is a **single stitched WebM** containing all scenes with transitions, written to the configured output path.

## Design decisions (producer answers)

- **Q1 — Scene-list specification:** **A (config file).** A JSON config file lists the scenes with their targets and play/capture durations.
- **Q2 — Scene target:** **"A now, C later".** First cut targets **gym scene keys** (Option A) via the dev-gated in-page director; the deferred Option C (generated shipped-game levels) is tracked as a follow-up work item — **AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX** — and is explicitly **out of scope** here.
- **Q3 — Fade rendering:** **A (page-side canvas overlay).** The fade is drawn over the canvas by the capture (Playwright injection), so the continuously-running `MediaRecorder` captures it and no game-side change is needed. Because one recorder runs across all scenes, scene switching must happen **in-page** (a page reload would end the recorder).

### Assumptions recorded

- Gym scene keys are stable and follow the `Gym<Name>` convention (`src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`).
- A 0.25 s fade at the capture's 60 fps is ≈ 15 frames in each direction; timing is derived from wall-clock, consistent with the existing capture tooling.
- Default output path follows the existing convention under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree.
- The watchable set of gym scenes excludes the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`; the director rejects them with a clear error.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new) — scene-list config parsing/validation, scene-plan/timing arithmetic, page-side fade overlay + director invocation, batch orchestration, single-output stitching.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` (new) — types for the scene-capture module's pure helpers.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (new) — hermetic tests for config validation, scene planning, fade timing, and director key validation.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — expose/reuse the existing server-boot, browser, recorder and probe plumbing (or add a `--scenes` mode) rather than duplicating it.
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (new) — dev-gated `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector` handle: validates keys against discovered gym scenes and calls `game.scene.start(key)`; inert in production.
- `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` (new) — unit tests for the pure key-validation logic and the dev gate.
- `src/core/boot.ts` — register the capture director at boot in dev builds only.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document the config schema, command and fade behaviour.
- `package.json` — `capture:scenes` script entry.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (Option C):** generated-level scenes are the literal brief but larger; recorded as a linked follow-up (**AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX**), not implemented here.
- **Dev-only subject matter:** gym scenes are not the shipped game, so the resulting video is a dev showcase rather than a marketing-accurate capture — acceptable for Option A; the Option C follow-up addresses this.
- **Gym playback caveats:** some gym scenes may rely on the gym-index context (back-to-index navigation) or a panel interaction; the director must be verified per scene, and unsupported scenes rejected rather than recorded blank.
- **Fade timing/overlay reliability under headless software WebGL** must be verified in the recorded output (not just assumed), since the probe samples frames.
- **Recorder lifetime:** the whole design depends on scene switching never reloading the page; the director must avoid navigation.
- **Assumption:** the existing `MediaRecorder`/probe/audio-tap machinery can be reused unchanged across scene switches.

## Related work

- **Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot)** (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — `completed`. The capture pipeline this builds on.
- **Create full video playthroughs** (AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU) — `completed`. Single full-run capture; distinct from multi-scene.
- **Compile an action video** (AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX) — `open`, `plan_complete`. `related-to:AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC` — edits **already-captured** footage with ffmpeg into a promo/showreel; this item **records new** multi-scene footage. Related, not a blocker.
- **Scripted Gameplay Videos: generated-level scenes (Option C follow-up)** (AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX) — `idea`, `discovered-from:AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC`. The deferred Option C.

## Appendix: Interview Q&A

- **Q1 (Map, to producer): How should the scene list be specified?** — **ANSWERED: A** — a JSON config file listing scenes with target and play/capture durations. Source: interactive reply (comment `AH-C0MV0GDIZE0080EX2`).
- **Q2 (Map, to producer): What does each scene target, and how is it started?** — **ANSWERED: "A now, C later"** — first cut targets gym scene keys (Option A) via a dev-gated in-page scene director; Option C (generated game levels) deferred to follow-up AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX. Expanded analysis: comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6`. Source: interactive reply (this session).
- **Q3 (Map, to producer): How should the fade-to-black / fade-from-black transitions be rendered?** — **ANSWERED: A** — page-side canvas overlay via Playwright. Source: interactive reply (comment `AH-C0MV0GDIZE0080EX2`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)
- **AH-0MVDV4DMY001Z7CU** – Capture: export action-intensity series + join anchor (open)
- **AH-0MV1CVC3O002DMM2** – C3: Multi-iteration capture loop — one server/browser, fresh page, continue-on-failure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: adds, answer, asked, batch, best (+203 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: adds, answer, answers, appendix, asked (+189 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: adds, best, boss, bot, canvas (+166 more)

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

# Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience

> **Headline:** Add a versioned, bot-baseline-derived **intended-experience
> targets** artifact plus a deterministic **human-experience validation**
> command that compares measured human (and bot) balance statistics against
> those bands, emitting a versioned JSON report and Markdown summary and
> failing with a non-zero exit code on drift.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing is currently a manual, point-in-time activity. The automated-balancing
framework produces a stable, versioned `BalanceReport`, and the human-play
statistics work item produces the *same* statistics for real players — but
nothing states what the experience is *supposed* to be, and nothing periodically
checks the measured experience against it. This item turns the bot batch into
the **source of truth for intended experience** (recorded as explicit target
bands and mirrored into the GDD), then adds a repeatable validation that flags
drift in the measured human experience.

## Users

- **As a game designer / producer**, I want a periodic report comparing the
  measured human experience against explicit intended-experience targets, so I
  can see whether the game still plays as designed and where it has drifted.
- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want the intended experience written
  down as machine-checkable targets derived from a bot baseline, so a tuning
  change can be judged against a recorded standard rather than remembered.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the same validation to run against a fresh bot
  batch, so a regression in the balance baseline is caught even before any human
  play is recorded.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, versioned pass/fail artifact, so the
  experience of the game can be reviewed over time.

## Intended-experience definition (decision recorded)

The operator chose the **bot baseline** as the source of intended-experience
targets, with the **GDD updated to match**. Concretely:

- A bot batch (`npm run evaluate -- --batch`) produces the shared
  `BalanceAggregate`. Its per-metric distributions define the **target band**
  (centre = baseline mean/median; tolerance = a documented multiple of std-dev
  or a relative percentage).
- The resulting bands are committed as a **versioned targets artifact** — the
  single machine-checkable statement of intended experience.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` is updated so the *prose* intended experience
  (survival, pacing, progression, reward cadence) agrees with those bands.

This keeps one source of truth (the artifact) and one narrative (the GDD).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Versioned, machine-checkable targets.** A targets artifact (e.g.
   `src/data/experience-targets.json`) records, for each key metric of the
   shared `BalanceAggregate` schema — at minimum `survivalSeconds`,
   `mineralsCollected`, `upgradesSelected`, `waveReached`, `levelReached` and
   `avoidableHits` — a target band (centre + tolerance) plus a version
   constant, seeded from a recorded bot batch baseline. A test asserts the
   artifact validates against the schema and covers every required metric.
- **Pure comparator.** A pure, clock-free, I/O-free module compares a
   `BalanceAggregate` (human **or** bot) against the targets and returns, per
   metric, the measured value, the target band, the signed drift magnitude and
   a pass/fail verdict. Unit tests cover in-band, above-band, below-band,
   missing-metric and empty-input cases, and assert no I/O / clock access.
- **Periodic validation command.** A documented on-demand command (e.g.
   `npm run validate-experience -- <balance-report.json>`) reads a
   `BalanceReport`, compares it against the targets, writes a **versioned JSON
   report** and a **Markdown summary**, and **exits non-zero when any metric
   drifts beyond tolerance**. It labels the source (human / bot policy) in the
   output. Its scheduling (e.g. a documented cron/CI recipe) is documented but
   not built as CI infrastructure in this item.
- **Determinism and reproducibility.** The same input report + targets yields
   byte-identical JSON and Markdown output; the pure core never reads the wall
   clock. Verified by tests (run twice, diff).
- **GDD, documentation and test suite.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` is
   updated so the intended experience matches the bot-baseline-derived targets;
   the validation workflow, targets artifact and report shape are documented
   (extending `docs/BALANCING.md` and/or a new `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md`
   plus code comments/README as applicable); and the **full project test suite
   passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Delivered dependency:** this item depends on **Collect balance statistics
  from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN), which is
  now **completed**, together with its helper child AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` exists). The human `BalanceReport` this
  validation consumes is therefore available; implementation may proceed.
- Reuse the shared schema (`BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`) — no schema
  duplication.
- **Dev tooling only:** the targets artifact and validator are development
  tooling; no production game-code call site, no telemetry/consent change.
- Deterministic and byte-stable output; the pure core must not read the wall
  clock or perform I/O.
- No wall-clock/network dependency in the comparator; the `--batch` path is
  already reproducible and must stay so.

## Existing state

- **Shared schema:** `src/ai/eval/types.ts` defines `DistributionStats`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`,
  `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION` and `EVAL_DATASET_VERSION`
  (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ, completed).
- **Bot batch:** `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` write a
  byte-stable `balance-report.json` / `.txt` / `runs.jsonl` under `--out`
  (default `eval-output/`), documented in `docs/BALANCING.md`. A recorded
  100-game baseline exists in that document's acceptance-verification section.
- **Human stats (delivered):** **Collect balance statistics from human
  player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, completed) emits a `BalanceReport`
  labelled with a `human` pseudo-policy. Its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) is present.
- **No targets, comparator or validation command exists today.**
- **Related tuning loop:** **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (
  AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715, open) covers baseline/compare for *tuning*; this item
  covers *periodic experience validation* against a committed standard.

## Desired change

1. Add a versioned targets artifact (schema + initial bot-baseline values) and
   a loader/validator.
2. Add a pure comparator module producing per-metric drift + verdicts.
3. Add the validation CLI and a `package.json` script.
4. Add the JSON + Markdown report writers (byte-stable).
5. Add tests (schema, comparator, CLI, determinism) and update docs + GDD.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — add target/drift types + version constant (or a new
  `experienceTargets.ts`).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.ts` — pure targets loader + comparator
  (new).
- `src/data/experience-targets.json` — versioned intended-experience bands
  seeded from a bot baseline (new; exact path TBD at implementation).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.test.ts` — schema + comparator unit tests
  (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — validation CLI (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.test.ts` — CLI + determinism tests (new).
- `package.json` — add the validation script.
- `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` and/or `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the
  workflow, targets and report shape.

  the targets.

  schema and batch runner.

  (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — supplies the human statistics (dependency).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** CI scheduling, dashboards and automatic ticket creation

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does a targets artifact or validator already exist?**

# Wormhole appears away from player

- **Type:** bug
- **Priority:** medium (as supplied at creation)

## Problem statement

At the start of each wave, `PlayScene.spawnWave()` opens the wormhole VFX at
the **first enemy's formation slot** (`spawns[0]`) while formations are laid
out in fixed **screen coordinates**. On waves whose formation ranges (or live
gameplay) place that slot near the player — or where the player has
moved/drifted up into the enemy zone — the wormhole can open right on or
beside the player ship, which is jarring and visually unfair. The wormhole
should appear at an **independent position well away** from the player's
current position and near-future trajectory, and the enemy formation should be
anchored **relative to the wormhole** rather than to the screen (producer
decision, Q1b/Q2a).

## Users

- **Primary: players** of the shipped game (`PlayScene`). "As a player I want
  the wave-opening wormhole to appear well away from my ship (and from where
  I'm heading), so enemies never seem to erupt on top of me."
- **Secondary: developers / gym users.** Per the gym↔game parity convention
  (AGENTS.md), the placement + anchoring rule must live once in shared code
  and be consumed identically by `PlayScene` and the gym formation scenes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Away from the player's current position** — When `spawnWave()` opens the
   wave wormhole, the chosen position's Euclidean distance from the player's
   live position is **≥ the largest of the wave's enemy-formation height or
   width** (`D_MIN = max(formation height, formation width)`, computed from
   the planned wave), whenever a conforming position exists.
2. **Away from the player's trajectory** — The same `D_MIN` also holds
   against the player's **projected position** a short horizon ahead (proposed
   ≈ the wormhole open+growth window, ~2 s) along the player's current
   velocity vector, so a moving player does not run into a freshly opened
   wormhole.
3. **Formation anchored to the wormhole** — Enemy formation positions are
   computed **relative to the wormhole position** (portal-relative offsets),
   not absolute screen coordinates, in both `PlayScene` and the gym formation
   scenes: wherever the portal opens, the formation hangs off it. A moved
   portal moves the whole formation with it. No change to spacing/pacing.
4. **Deterministic placement, safe fallback** — Placement is a pure function
   of (formation geometry, playfield bounds, player state) and is
   unit-testable with an injected RNG (pattern: `src/powerups/placement.ts`).
   When no in-bounds candidate meets `D_MIN`, the furthest-available candidate
   is used and the position is still never placed inside the player's hull
   radius + a small safety margin.
5. **Gym↔game parity** — The placement/anchor helper lives in the shared
   layer (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` or a sibling shared module) and both
   `PlayScene` and every gym formation scene call the same code path. Gyms
   have no player ship, so they pass no player: the portal stays at the
   formation base and the formation is already base-relative (behaviour
   unchanged in gyms). No regressions to the single-live wormhole lifecycle
   (AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6).
6. **Regression tests** — Deterministic tests (fail-before/pass-after) cover:
   (a) player centred / portal pick; (b) a candidate near the player is
   rejected; (c) a moving player with non-zero velocity (trajectory
   projection); (d) no-safe-candidate fallback; (e) the formation follows a
   translated portal (portal-relative anchoring); (f) gym scenes unchanged
   (formation base).
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the change —
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2.7 (wormhole spawn animation)
   and relevant code comments.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wormhole timing contract is unchanged: 1 s open + 1.5 s grow + 0.5 s
  close = 3 s spawn-protection window (existing constants in
  `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`); the trajectory-projection horizon is a small
  documented constant.
- The formation **anchor** changes (portal-relative), but enemy **spacing,
  offsets, count and wave pacing** are unchanged.
- The formation extent used for `D_MIN` must come from a single source
  derived from the planned wave (not hard-coded per call site).
- Do not break the deterministic test seams used by the scene suites
  (`finishSpawnAnimations()`, `scene.tick(dt)`).

## Existing state

- `PlayScene.spawnWave()` opens the wormhole at `spawns[0]` (the first enemy
  slot) via `this._wormhole.open(spawns[0].x, spawns[0].y, wormholeEffects)` —
  no player-awareness at all.
- `waveManager.planSpawns(rng)` → `planGroupSpawns()` computes each group's
  base position from screen-coordinate ranges (`startX/startY` ± `startXMin/
  startXMax` etc.) and spreads formation offsets from that base
  (`computeFormationPosition`).
- Gym formation scenes open the wormhole at the formation base
  (`_resolveFormationBase()` → `formationBaseX/Y`) and already lay the
  formation out relative to that base; gyms have no player ship (`GymPlayer`
  is a DOM config panel, not an in-game ship).
- The player starts at `(GAME_WIDTH/2, GAME_HEIGHT-80)` in a 960×540
  playfield and moves freely; its live position and velocity vector
  (`MovementState.vx/vy`) are queryable from `this.player`.
- Reusable precedent: `src/powerups/placement.ts` (`RandomAvoidingPlacement`,
  AH-0MU44M90T003EQ2G) solves "random on-screen spot avoiding bodies, with
  injected RNG and deterministic fallback" for power-up drops.

## Desired change

- Introduce a shared `placeWavePortal(player, formationExtents, playfield)`
  helper (pure, RNG-injected, Phaser-independent for unit testing) that
  returns a position satisfying AC1–AC2, plus the shared formation-anchoring
  step (AC3): translate the planned formation offsets from the portal.
- `PlayScene.spawnWave()`: (1) derive the wave's formation extents (from the
  spawn plan / group geometry), (2) choose the portal position via the shared
  helper with the live player position + velocity, (3) open the wormhole
  there, (4) anchor every group/formation base to the portal position instead
  of the screen ranges.
- Gym formation scenes: call the same shared helper without a player
  (portal = formation base) so both scenes share one code path; gym behaviour
  is unchanged.
- Add the horizon constant and `D_MIN` derivation to the shared module,
  documented with the producer-approved rule (largest of formation height or
  width).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — shared `placeWavePortal` helper + horizon /
  `D_MIN` constants (pure, RNG-injected).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `planGroupSpawns()`/group bases become
  portal-relative (or expose formation extents + offset plan for anchoring);
  formation-extent derivation.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `spawnWave()`: portal choice (live player) +
  formation anchoring instead of `spawns[0]`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — route `_spawnFormation()`
  through the shared helper (no player → formation base, unchanged
  behaviour).
- `src/powerups/placement.ts` — reference pattern only (reuse
  `RandomAvoidingPlacement` style; no change expected).
- Tests: `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` (helper: geometry, trajectory,
  fallback, RNG determinism), `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (scene-level
  AC1–AC3, e), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` /
  `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` (parity, f), WaveManager tests if bases change.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §2.7 placement + anchoring
  note.

## Related work

- **AH-0MURBER4L00821RR** (completed) — wormhole VFX + growth + spawn
  protection; this item refines where the VFX opens and anchors the formation
  to it.
- **AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6** (completed, in_review) — wormhole lifecycle
  (single-live controller); repositioning must not regress the lifecycle
  invariants (close-on-open, idempotent close).
- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (open) — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole";
  sibling aesthetics item. Interaction: with the producer's Q1b decision, the
  portal is decoupled from the formation and the formation is anchored to it —
  the sibling's "enemies start at the wormhole position" follows directly and
  its traversal distances are bounded by the portal-anchored formation.
  Noted, not blocking, do not absorb.
- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** (open) — "Create an improved Phase Shift effect"
  (wormhole-exit) — cosmetic, not blocking.
- **AH-0MU44M90T003EQ2G** (completed) — "Pluggable avoiding placement
  strategy" and **AH-0MU7JTFM5000R4ME** (completed) — "Power-ups spawn too
  close together" — the reusable placement pattern
  (`src/powerups/placement.ts`) this item should follow.
- AGENTS.md "Gym↔game parity" convention.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Resolved (Q1):** placement strategy = **independent portal position** with
  the **formation anchored relative to the portal** (producer decision).
- **Resolved (Q2):** "well away" = **`D_MIN` = the largest of the enemy
  formation's height or width** (producer decision), Euclidean distance, from
  the player's current position and its ~2 s trajectory-projected position.
- **Assumption:** trajectory-projection horizon ≈ 2 s (the wormhole open+growth
  window) — a small documented constant, easily tuned.
- **Assumption:** absolute (not squared) Euclidean distance for `D_MIN`;
  margin/hull constant for the never-inside fallback.
- **Assumption:** gyms keep the formation-base portal (no player ship to
  avoid); parity is satisfied by one shared code path with an optional player.
- **Risk:** formation re-anchoring touches wave planning
  (`planGroupSpawns`/bases) — broad blast radius across formation tests.
  Mitigation: shared translation, deterministic fail-before/pass-after tests.
- **Risk:** large formations (march block, horde) may never meet `D_MIN` in
  the playfield — the determinist fallback (furthest-available) is exercised
  and tested.
- **Risk:** very fast player movement may make the trajectory projection
  over/under-conservative. Mitigation: conservative horizon + worst-case
  velocity test + exposed constant.
- **Scope creep:** enemy-exit traversal (AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW), wormhole
  lifecycle fidelity (AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6) and Phase Shift VFX
  (AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S) are tracked separately — out of scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where may the wave wormhole open when its default position (first enemy
  slot) is too close to the player?" —
  - (a) Anchor to the **farthest formation slot** from the player. **Recommended
    (agent):** (a) — minimal change, keeps the portal diegetically tied to the
    formation.
  - (b) Choose an **independent** far-away position in the playfield — with the
    refinement that the **formation location becomes relative to the portal
    position, not the screen position**.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "(b) — formation location should
    be relative to the portal position not the screen position." Final accepted:
    (b) with the formation-anchored refinement.
- Q2: "What distance counts as 'well away' from the player?" —
  - (a) A fixed constant with a trajectory projection. **Recommended (agent):**
    (a), proposed default ~200 px.
  - (b) A screen fraction (e.g. ≥ ⅓ of screen height).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "(a) — where the distance is
    calculated from the largest of the height or width of the enemy
    formations." Final accepted: (a), with `D_MIN` = max(formation height,
    formation width) replacing the 200 px default.
- Research summary: inspected `PlayScene.spawnWave()` / `_spawnEnemy()`,
  `WaveManager.planGroupSpawns()` / `computeFormationPosition`,
  `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation()` / `_resolveFormationBase()`,
  `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/entities/Player.ts` (movement state exposes
  `vx/vy`), and the completed power-up placement pattern
  `src/powerups/placement.ts` (AH-0MU44M90T003EQ2G). No existing
  player-distance handling for the wormhole was found; the two answers above
  resolve the only design forks not answerable from the seed context or repo.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MURBER4L00821RR** – Spawning enemies enter from a wormhole and grow from 1 pixel to their full size (completed)
- **AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2** – Level-up offers duplicate weapon (basic + upgraded version of same weapon) (completed — keyword false-positive; not related)
- **AH-0MU7JTFM5000R4ME** – Power-ups spawn too close together (completed — placement precedent)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — wormhole/wave/player/trajectory docs to update (§2.7)
- `README.md` — matched on generic gameplay terms; no change expected
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched on generic gameplay terms; no change expected

# Enemies should emerge from the wormhole

## Problem statement

When enemies spawn at the start of a wave they appear directly at their formation positions and only grow in scale. They should instead emerge from the centre of the wormhole and move (traverse) to their starting position, completing the movement within the spawn-protection window so the player cannot hit them until they arrive.

## Users

- **Primary:** Players experiencing the game — "As a player I expect enemies to arrive through the wormhole and move to their positions, so the spawn feels cinematic and diegetic rather than popping into existence."
- **Secondary:** Gym scene users — parity requires the same movement behaviour in all gym scenes that spawn enemies.

## Acceptance Criteria


- **Movement from wormhole to formation** — Each spawned enemy starts at the wormhole position (the same position where the wormhole VFX opens) and moves linearly to its configured formation position over the spawn-protection window.
- **Timing matches protection window** — The movement completes within the existing 3-second spawn-protection window (1 s open + 1.5 s grow + 0.5 s close), so enemies are fully arrived before the wormhole closes and before they become collidable.
- **Spawn protection during transit** — While moving from the wormhole, enemies retain spawning protection: player bullets pass through, no shooting, no body collision, no mineral absorption (existing gates on `isSpawning` apply).
- **Parity across scenes** — The same movement behaviour is applied consistently to both `PlayScene` (the main game) and all gym scenes that spawn enemies.
- **All tests pass** — The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
## Constraints

- The movement must not change the spawn positions or timing of enemies — only the visual and positional presentation during the spawn sequence.
- The animation must work for all enemy types (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid, Harvester).
- Movement must be smooth and visually pleasing (linear interpolation with optional easing).
- The enemy must reach its formation position before or exactly when the spawn-protection window ends.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy()` instantiates each enemy at its formation position (`spawn.x`, `spawn.y`) via `createEnemyFromConfig()` and starts the wormhole growth animation.
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation()` instantiates each entity at its formation slot position via the config factory and similarly starts the growth animation.
- The wormhole VFX opens at the first enemy's spawn position (`spawns[0].x, spawns[0].y`) in `PlayScene.spawnWave()` and at the formation base (`this.formationBaseX, this.formationBaseY`) in gyms.
- Enemies currently grow in scale at their formation positions — no positional movement from the wormhole.

## Desired change

- Modify `_spawnEnemy` (PlayScene) and `_spawnFormation` (GymFormationScene) so enemies start at the wormhole position and move toward their formation position during the spawn animation.
- Use the existing `SpawnState` / `updateSpawnAnimation` helpers to drive the movement alongside the scale growth.
- Both scenes use the same 3-second protection window; movement must complete within it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — Extend `SpawnState` with a destination position; update `updateSpawnAnimation` to handle positional movement.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy()`: start enemies at wormhole position (not formation position), set destination to formation position.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation()`: same pattern as PlayScene.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — No changes expected; `isSpawning` gates already cover movement.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Update §2.7 to document the movement phase.
- Tests in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — Cover movement from wormhole to position.

## Related work

- **AH-0MURBER4L00821RR** (completed) — "Spawning enemies enter from a wormhole and grow from 1 pixel to their full size" — implemented the wormhole VFX, scale growth, and spawn-protection gates. This work item extends that feature with positional movement.
- **AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6** (completed, in_review) — "Wormhole stays visible on some waves" — fixed wormhole lifecycle; not blocking.
- **AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC** (in-progress) — "Wormhole appears away from player" — different symptom (wormhole positioning), not blocking.
- AGENTS.md "Gym↔game parity" convention — the parity requirement for this change.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** Linear movement from wormhole to formation position is the correct approach; no curved paths or spirals required unless specified.
- **Assumption:** All enemies in a wave emerge from the same wormhole position (the first enemy's position in the game, the formation base in gyms).
- **Risk:** Long-range enemies (e.g. distant formation positions) may make the movement too obvious or slow; easing or variable speed may be needed.
- **Risk:** The Diver entity already has complex movement (dive phase, re-anchor glide); the spawn movement must not interfere with its existing animation pipeline.
- **Scope creep:** Avoid adding particle trails or extra VFX on the moving enemy unless explicitly requested.

# Create an improved Phase Shift effect

## Problem statement

The current Phase Shift treatment — a static dark-blue desaturation overlay plus a
cyan/red chromatic split — is not distinctive enough: when the ship phases out the
player has to look for a subtle tint to confirm it, and enemies arriving out of the
wormhole carry no visual warning at all that they are "not fully here". The ask is a
"shimmer" and "glitch" read so a phased entity is unmistakably in a different state.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, when my ship phases out — or when enemies
  emerge from the wormhole at the start of a wave — I want them to shimmer and glitch
  so it is instantly obvious they are not in their usual state."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the auto Phase Shift, I want the
  effect to visibly 'fire' at the moment of activation so I can trust it and time my
  flying accordingly."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want the shimmer/glitch behaviour to
  live once in the shared core/VFX layer so the shipped game and every combat gym look
  identical and cannot diverge (gym↔game parity convention)."

Example user stories:

- *"My ship phased out mid-bullet-hell and I didn't even notice — I want the screen to
  ripple and shimmer the instant phase fires, then keep pulsing so I know the state is
  still on."*
- *"Scouts poured out of the wormhole and I couldn't tell they were materialising — I
  want each one to flicker and glow as it grows, so I read 'not solid yet'."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Player phase activation burst (glitch).** On the frame the Phase Shift activates (`isPhased` rising edge) the screen-wide treatment emits a brief **ripple/burst** — e.g. a short sharp chromatic-split surge with a flicker step — that reads as a "glitch" hit, distinct from the player-death juice (no camera shake; the existing screen-wide overlays are retained).
- **Continuous player shimmer while phased.** While `isPhased` stays true the treatment sustains a **continuous shimmer**: the existing cyan/red chromatic split becomes **more vivid and pulsing** — higher alpha (raised from 0.10 toward ~0.20), wider offset (raised from 3 px toward ~6 px) with a slow oscillation — plus a subtle alpha flicker (≈2–4 Hz) and a soft colour-pulse between the two split hues. All magnitudes exported as tunable constants with per-layer `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggles (mirroring the current `phaseShiftJuice` pattern). Phase expiry clears every layer on the falling edge, leaving no residual tint.
- **Per-enemy shimmer/glitch during wormhole emergence (no screen-space effects).** Each enemy growing from the wormhole gets a **per-entity** treatment over its growth window (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`): a brief ripple burst as it starts to materialise, then a continuous shimmer — a subtle scale/alpha flicker plus a soft colour-pulse on the entity itself — all driven from the shared spawn-animation path (`updateSpawnAnimation`) so `PlayScene` and every gym behave identically. No screen-wide overlay is introduced for the emergence path.
- **Wormhole-position glow/pulse ring.** While a wormhole is open for a wave the wormhole itself gets a subtle glow/pulse ring (radius pulse + soft glow at the wormhole position, drawn once per wormhole, tracked in the existing `wormholeEffects` registry and cleared when the wormhole closes). Visually distinct from both the phase-shift treatment and the player-death juice.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover: pure params model (new tunables mapped verbatim, toggles honoured), activation burst + continuous shimmer layer creation/teardown (edge-triggered, no residual layers), per-enemy shimmer driven by the spawn-state window, wormhole ring lifecycle, the no-camera-shake regression for Phase Shift, and safe-no-op behaviour headless. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (juice) is updated with the new shimmer/glitch treatment and tunables, and code comments document every new constant. The full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **No camera shake** (established producer decision — shake made Phase Shift read
  like player-death juice; the regression test asserting "never shakes" stays).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the shimmer/glitch behaviour lives once in the
  shared core/VFX layer (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`,
  the shared `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` spawn path) and is consumed by both
  `PlayScene` and the gyms — no divergent copies (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity
  docs assertion apply).
- **Screen-wide effects only for the player phase path.** The enemy-emergence path is
  per-entity/per-wormhole only — the producer explicitly chose "no screen space
  effects" for spawning enemies.
- Keep the existing cyan/red split identity (producer Q3 = A: more vivid, not
  recoloured); keep per-layer toggles and the pure `resolve*Params()` pattern.
- Safe no-op without a Phaser render context (headless tests); no new runtime
  dependencies; performance-neutral (tweens/alpha only, no per-frame allocations
  beyond the existing pattern).

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — screen-wide Phase Shift treatment: dark-blue
  dim overlay (α 0.22) + cyan/red chromatic split (α 0.1, 3 px offset), edge-triggered
  `update(active, dt)` (the `dt` param is currently unused — reserved for pulsing).
  Camera-shake regression and pure-param tests in `phaseShiftJuice.test.ts`.
- `CombatCoreScene._updatePhaseShiftJuice(dt)` lazily constructs the controller and
  drives it from `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased` — shared by `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`.
- `applyPhaseGhost` (`CombatEffectVisuals.ts`) sets the ship ghost alpha while phased
  (unchanged; per-entity shimmer is additive and must not fight it).
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — wormhole open (1 s) → enemy growth
  (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` = 1.5 s via `startSpawnAnimation`/`updateSpawnAnimation`/
  `isEnemySpawning`) → close (0.5 s); `WormholeController` guarantees at most one live
  wormhole; `spawnWormholeOpen/Close` handles.
- `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each drive spawn updates from `updateSpawnAnimation`
  and open/close the single wormhole from `this._wormhole` with the `wormholeEffects`
  registry (`CombatScene.wormholeEffects`, cleared on `SHUTDOWN`).

## Desired change

- In `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`: raise split alpha/offset and add a slow pulsing
  oscillation and an activation ripple/burst + continuous shimmer/flicker layer, all
  under tunables/toggles; keep edge-triggered apply/clear and the no-shake guarantee.
- In `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`: add per-entity shimmer/glitch helpers driven from the
  spawn-growth window (burst on growth start, then flicker/pulse while growing), and a
  wormhole glow/pulse ring tied to the wormhole's open lifetime.
- Wire the per-entity shimmer into the shared spawn path so `PlayScene` and the gyms
  consume it identically; wire the wormhole ring into the existing `wormholeEffects`
  registry lifecycle.
- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 and code comments; extend the unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — **Edit**: vivid/pulsing split, activation burst,
  continuous shimmer layers, new tunables/toggles.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — **Edit**: params, burst/shimmer, no-shake, edge
  trigger, teardown.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — **Edit**: per-enemy shimmer/glitch helpers +
  wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — **Edit**: new helper tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: any
  shared wiring needed to drive the new effects (e.g. pass spawn state, ring
  lifecycle) without divergent copies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the shared emergence-path
  helpers; no new behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the same
  shared helpers (parity).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 juice description + new tunables.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Over-stimulation / seizure sensitivity* — shimmer, flicker and glitch bursts can be
  uncomfortable. Mitigation: keep magnitudes small and durations short, drive every
  layer from exported tunables with per-layer toggles (consistent with existing juice
  practice); player shimmer uses a gentle ≈2–4 Hz flicker, not rapid strobe; a
  reduce-motion accessibility option is out of scope here (separate tracked idea).
- *Player-death overlap* — the burst must not read as death juice. Mitigation: keep
  the no-camera-shake regression, reuse the chromatic-split identity only (never the
  death ring/flash palette), and keep the burst short (~150–250 ms).
- *Parity drift* — PlayScene/gym copies diverge. Mitigation: implement once in the
  shared core/VFX modules; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs
  assertion enforce this.
- *Per-frame cost* — pulsing/flicker must not allocate per frame. Mitigation: use
  Phaser tweens and existing object reuse; no new particle emitters beyond the ring.
- *Scope creep* — the "glitch" ask could balloon into post-processing shaders.
  Mitigation: keep to the current overlay/entity technique (no render-to-texture or
  shader work); record any shader-grade effect as a separate linked item.

**Assumptions** (producer-validated via Q1–Q3)

- *Player shimmer/glitch* = activation burst then continuous shimmer, **with** the
  existing screen-wide treatment retained and made more vivid/pulsing (producer: "for
  players D — with screen space effects"; Q3 = A).
- *Emerging enemies* = per-entity shimmer/glitch (burst + shimmer) **without** any
  screen-wide effect, plus a subtle wormhole-position glow/pulse ring (producer:
  "spawning enemies D — no screen space effects"; "B + wormhole effect — no screen
  space effects").
- The existing cyan/red split palette is retained (vivid, not recoloured).
- The ship's ghost alpha (`applyPhaseGhost`) is unchanged; per-entity shimmer is
  applied to emergent enemies only, not to the player's ship object itself.
- The effect is purely cosmetic: gameplay, hitboxes and spawn protection are
  unchanged.

## Related work

See the automated "Related work (automated report)" section below (added by the
`find-related` skill).

- Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8) — *completed*;
  parent of the existing automatic Phase Shift and its juice module.
- Phase Shift juice module (AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS) — *completed*; the module this work
  upgrades (screen-wide dim + chromatic split, no shake).
- PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual (AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5) — *completed*; the
  ship ghost-alpha precedent (`applyPhaseGhost`).
- Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice) (AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) —
  *completed*; reference for a layered, toggleable juice module and the defeat glitch
  flicker pattern.
- P6 charge and permanent auto-trigger model (AH-0MUJRGVQE004XA1T) — *completed*;
  introduced the Phase Shift auto-trigger the juice must clearly communicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What specific visual effects should 'shimmer' and 'glitch' include?** Options:
  (A) rapid alpha flickering + colour cycling on the existing overlays; (B) screen-space
  distortion (pixel displacement / chromatic aberration wobble); (C) per-entity
  ripple/burst on activation + noise-like overlay flicker; (D) combination: brief
  ripple burst on activation, then continuous shimmer (flicker + subtle colour pulse).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **D for spawning enemies (no screen space
  effects), D for players (with screen space effects).** Rationale: a brief burst on
  activation gives the 'glitch' hit, then a continuous shimmer maintains the state
  read; the agent's recommended option was D.
- **Q2 — Should enemies emerging from the wormhole receive the same screen-wide phase
  treatment or a per-enemy effect?** Options: (A) same screen-wide effect; (B) per-enemy
  personal shimmer/glow as it grows; (C) wormhole-position glow/pulse ring + standard
  screen-wide effect when phase-shift is active.
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B + wormhole effect — no screen space
  effects.** Rationale: per-entity shimmer/glow during growth plus a subtle wormhole
  ring, with no screen-wide overlays on the emergence path.
- **Q3 — Colour palette/style for the shimmer/glitch?** Options: (A) keep the existing
  cyan/red split but more vivid (higher alpha, wider offset, pulsing); (B) purple/violet
  palette (wormhole colours); (C) neutral desaturated + subtle RGB-shift (CRT).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A.** Rationale: preserve the established
  phase-shift identity while making it clearly more visible; the agent's recommended
  option was A.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTE8EBVD0010T0Z** – Unit tests: P6 Phase Shift - pass-through, expiry, refresh (completed)
- **AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN** – Respawn player in same spot (completed)
- **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** – Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, activates, activation, active, add (+373 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, acceptance, activates, activation, active (+350 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, activates, active, add, added (+310 more)

# Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff

> **Headline:** Add a `--tune` mode to the batch-evaluation CLI that runs a
> baseline batch, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs the *identical*
> sweep and writes a versioned before/after comparison with per-metric deltas
> and a readable summary — so a tuning attempt becomes one auditable,
> repeatable command instead of a manual chore.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) provides the *evidence*
(batch reports with distribution statistics) but the *loop* around it is still
manual and error-prone. A designer who wants to tune a knob must, by hand:
(1) run a baseline batch, (2) edit a CSV, (3) re-run the identical command,
(4) diff the JSON/text reports and interpret per-metric deltas across a table
of distributions. Human error creeps in exactly where the tool exists to remove
it: forgetting to keep seeds identical, comparing reports from different batch
configs, or misreading which metrics actually moved. The acceptance-verification
run already had to do this diff by hand (see docs/BALANCING.md §Acceptance-verification run).

There is no automation that: records a baseline, applies a single proposed edit
(guided), re-runs against the *same* seeds/config, and produces a per-metric
before/after comparison with guidance on whether each delta looks like the
intended effect.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run one command that (baseline → edit → re-run → compare) reports exactly which balance metrics moved and by how much, so tuning becomes a fast, auditable loop instead of a manual chore.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, repeatable record of each tuning attempt (edit, config snapshot, before/after reports) so balance history can be reviewed and reverted.

## Expected behaviour

- A `--tune` mode on the existing `scripts/evaluate.mjs` entry point (Q1-b)
  that:
  1. Runs the baseline batch (identical seeds/config/policy) and captures the report.
  2. Applies a single, **declarative** CSV edit supplied by the caller
     (e.g. `--set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=6`) — Q2-a; the tool can
     **restore** the original file on completion so the checkout stays clean.
  3. Re-runs the identical batch and emits a **before/after comparison**
     artifact (per-metric deltas: mean/median/stdDev per distribution, plus
     per-archetype kill and per-upgrade deltas) alongside both full reports.
  4. Prints a human-readable summary identifying the metrics that moved beyond
     a **relative ±10% default threshold** on mean/median (configurable via
     `--threshold`) — Q3-a — and flags distribution-shape changes (e.g. stdDev
     growth = variance increase, median shifts).
- No production runtime impact; all new logic stays in the dev/eval layer
  (`src/ai/eval/`, Node shell). Determinism guarantees are preserved
  byte-for-byte.

## Suggested approach

- Reuse the existing irreproducibility guard: the comparison must verify both batches used identical sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) before reporting deltas — an empty diff check confirms no side effects.
- Pure diff/aggregation logic in the TS core (`src/ai/eval/`) with a thin shell wrapper in `scripts/evaluate.mjs`; no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (same constraint as the epic).
- Where CSV edit support lands, reuse the shared loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` via `hydrateBalanceConfig` from `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts`) so the re-run reads the edited values.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: One-command loop.** A documented `--tune` command runs baseline, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs with an identical sweep, and writes three artifacts: baseline report, candidate report, and a versioned before/after comparison (per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas, per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas).
- **AC2: Same-sweep guard.** The tool refuses to compare batches whose sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) differs, and errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs (detects side effects).
- **AC3: Deterministic comparison.** Same edit + same seeds yields a byte-identical comparison artifact; independently-derived (empty) deltas are zero.
- **AC4: Safe restore.** After the run the CSV is byte-identical to its pre-run state on success **and** failure paths (or the user opted into keeping the edit), verified by test; the working tree is clean unless the user says otherwise.
- **AC5: Readable summary.** The text output flags metrics that moved beyond a configurable threshold (relative ±10% mean/median default) and notes distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), with the same statistics echoed in the machine-readable artifact.
- **AC6: Tests.** Pure comparison/aggregation, the same-sweep guard, safe restore and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC7: Documentation.** `docs/BALANCING.md` gains a `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section with the worked example; README references it.
- **AC8: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/EVALUATION.md` if the CLI flags there are extended).

## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a seed; no wall clock; the before/after comparison is reproducible byte-for-byte for the same edit + seeds.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock); filesystem work (CSV edit/restore, artifact writes) stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The re-run reads the edited values through the shared config loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `hydrateBalanceConfig`), never a divergent copy.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any shared gameplay behaviour exercised by the tune loop must come from the shared core; the tune loop is a dev tool like the gyms.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Two batches (baseline + candidate) must not exhaust memory; reuse the batch runner's incremental aggregation.
- **Checkout hygiene.** The CSV restore must leave the working tree clean on success **and** failure unless the user opts in to keeping the edit (AC4).

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — thin Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O); already parses `--batch`, `--games`, `--policies`, `--seed(s)`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`, `--json`; writes `balance-report.json`, `balance-report.txt`, `runs.jsonl` under `--out` (default `eval-output/`, git-ignored).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — `runBatch` sweeps seeds × policies deterministically; the batch config (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) is recorded in `BatchOutput.json`.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.ts`-family extraction (`metrics.ts`) and aggregation; `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`-versioned `BalanceRunStats` / `BalanceAggregate` (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`) with `DistributionStats` (count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev), per-archetype `enemiesKilledByArchetype` and per-upgrade `upgradesSelected`.
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — stable serialisation + human-readable summary.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — `hydrateBalanceConfig()` loads the real `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `ship-config.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`; `ENEMY_CSV_PATH` etc. exported.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — documents the batch runner; its §Acceptance-verification run shows the (manual) CSV-edit diff that this item automates.
- The batch report already hashes the config and records seeds, so the same-sweep guard's inputs exist today.

## Desired change

1. Extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode (Q1-b) that chains baseline → single declarative edit → re-run → compare in one command.
2. Add declarative CSV-edit support (`--set <file>.<field>=<value>`, Q2-a) with guaranteed restore (AC4).
3. Add pure diff/aggregation logic in `src/ai/eval/` producing a versioned before/after comparison artifact (per-metric deltas, per-archetype/per-upgrade deltas).
4. Emit a human-readable summary flagging metrics moved beyond the configurable ±10% relative threshold and noting shape changes (stdDev/median) (AC5).
5. Enforce the same-sweep guard (AC2) and determinism (AC3).
6. Document the tuning loop in `docs/BALANCING.md` with the worked example; reference from README (AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — new `--tune` mode: orchestrate baseline/edit/re-run/compare, CSV edit + restore, artifact writes (shell layer only).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` or new `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` — pure tuning-loop core: same-sweep guard, before/after comparison + aggregation, determinism.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — versioned before/after comparison types (deltas per metric/archetype/upgrade).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — comparison rendering (readable summary + stable JSON).
- `src/util/csvEdit.ts` (new, shell-adjacent) — declarative single-field CSV edit with restore; or handled inside the `.mjs` shell.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — reused via `hydrateBalanceConfig` so the re-run reads edited values.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — new `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section; README reference.
- Tests: new unit tests alongside `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` / `report.test.ts`; CLI shell tests next to `scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **Epic: Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — completed; this item closes the loop around it.
- **Extend the headless arena to the full campaign** (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) — open; once landed, per-wave/per-upgrade fields in the schema become populated and the tune loop's per-upgrade deltas become fully meaningful; not blocking this item (the loop diffs whatever the arena reports).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — in progress; the tune loop and the validation share the same versioned balance-statistics schema and will interoperate (tune → re-baseline → validate).
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — completed; shared schema consumer.

(Also see the automated related-work report appended to the item description.)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: CSV edit corrupts the checkout.** Mitigated by AC4 (restore on success and failure paths, tested; explicit opt-out to keep the edit).
- **Risk: comparing incompatible batches produces misleading deltas.** Mitigated by AC2 same-sweep guard (refuse on differing seeds/policies/ticks/dt/sampleEveryTicks) plus the empty byte-diff side-effect check.
- **Risk: "the intended effect" is subjective.** The tool reports and flags, it does not assert intent; the threshold default (±10% relative on mean/median) is configurable and documented.
- **Risk: scope creep** (interactive edit prompt, multi-edit batches, auto-apply best candidate, wave/upgrade tuning once the campaign arena lands). Recorded as follow-up opportunities, not in scope here.
- **Assumption: the current arena output is sufficient** for a useful first tuning loop (wave/upgrade fields may still be unpopulated until AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A; per-archetype and minerals/survival deltas are already meaningful).
- **Assumption: `--tune` reuses the existing batch flags** (`--games`, `--policies`, `--seeds`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`) with no new sweep semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Entry point — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode, or add a new peer `scripts/balance-tune.mjs`? **Recommended:** peer script (clearer separation)." — Answer (operator): "b" — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q2: "Edit interface for v1 — declarative `--set` only, or also an interactive prompt? **Recommended:** declarative `--set` only (deterministic, scriptable, testable without a TTY)." — Answer (operator): "a" — declarative `--set` only for v1; interactive prompt deferred. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q3: "'Moved significantly' default threshold — relative ±10% of baseline mean/median, absolute per-metric defaults, or relative + stdDev growth flag? **Recommended:** relative ±10% (scale-free across metrics)." — Answer (operator): "a" — relative ±10% default on mean/median, configurable via `--threshold`; stdDev/median shape-flagging retained per AC5. Source: interactive reply, this session.
