# MysteryUfoDrone collector entity

## Summary

Implement the visible collector drone as a shared-core entity: a code-drawn
scaled copy of the player ship that seeks minerals, vacuums them within its
collector radius, returns home and pays out.

## Target outcome

`src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` is a self-contained neon-vector entity with
the full seek → collect → return → payout lifecycle, lifetime/capacity
termination, and the agreed destruction contract.

## Minimal implementation

- New `MysteryUfoDrone` entity following the `Harvester` seek pattern
  (`setSeekTargets` + nearest-live-mineral steering) and the code-drawn
  graphics convention (no external art).
- Constructor takes the resolved level values (lifetime, capacity, radius).
- State machine: SEEK → COLLECT (vacuum minerals whose centre enters the
  radius) → RETURN (when full or lifetime expires) → PAYOUT → gone.
- Expose read-only accessors for tests (state, held minerals, target).
- Destruction contract: `onEnemyBullet`/`onEnemyBody` mark it destroyed and
  expose held minerals for the drop; a player-bullet check is a no-op.
- Unit tests (`MysteryUfoDrone.test.ts`) for the lifecycle and destruction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Level-0 drone: lifetime 5 s, capacity 10 minerals, collector radius 20 px,
  all overridable from resolved level data.
- The drone actively seeks the nearest live mineral, collects minerals whose
  centre enters its collector radius, returns to the player and pays out
  when it has collected its capacity **or** its lifetime expires (whichever
  comes first), and disappears after payout — verified by unit tests
  asserting the seek → collect → return → pay out flow.
- Termination fires on either capacity reached **or** lifetime expiry,
  whichever comes first, and the drone disappears after payout with exactly
  the held minerals in the pay-in.
- An enemy bullet or enemy body collision destroys the drone and exposes its
  held minerals for the drop; the player's own fire cannot destroy it.
- The drone is rendered as a scaled-down player-ship entity, code-drawn
  neon-vector, no external art.

## Parent AC covered

Covers parent AC2 (seek/collect/return/payout flow, lifetime/capacity
termination, level-0 defaults) and the destruction behaviour of AC5.

# Shared-core drone lifecycle pass

## Summary

Add the shared spawn/tick/teardown pass over the drone in the shared core so
the game and every gym run one identical implementation (gym↔game parity).

## Target outcome

A `src/scenes/core/` helper (mirroring `dropLayer.ts` / `mineralLayer.ts`)
that spawns drones, feeds them the live mineral field each tick, drains their
earned minerals into the scene's hold and converts a destroyed drone into
field deposits.

## Minimal implementation

- New shared helper (e.g. `combatDrone.ts`) with `spawnDrone`, `tickDrones`,
  `drainPayouts` and `teardownDrones`-style functions, pure where possible.
- Feed the live mineral field to each drone through `setSeekTargets`
  (reuse `enemyTargeting.pushSeekTargets` style) each shared tick.
- Route the drone's pay-in minerals into the caller-supplied hold sink; on
  destruction, drop held minerals plus a `2 × level` bonus as collectable
  field deposits via the existing mineral/drop layer.
- Wire the pass into `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` ordering so both
  `PlayScene` and gyms inherit it.
- Tests for spawn/tick/payout/destruction-drop at the helper level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The helper is the only place drone spawn/tick/teardown/payout logic lives;
  no per-scene copy exists (verified by the duplicate-body guard).
- Feeding the live mineral field makes the drone actively seek the nearest
  live mineral and collect minerals whose centre enters its collector
  radius; an empty field clears its target and it holds station.
- Payout minerals reach the supplied hold sink exactly once per drone when
  it returns to the player.
- On destruction by an enemy bullet or enemy body collision, the drone drops
  its held minerals plus a `2 × level` mineral bonus at its position,
  landing as collectable field deposits (verified at helper level).

## Parent AC covered

Covers the shared-core payout/destruction-drop mechanics of parent AC2/AC5
(in shared core, consumed identically by game and gyms).

# Tune-comparison core: versioned before/after deltas

> **Headline:** Pure diff/aggregation core for the `--tune` loop (child of AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715). Computes the versioned before/after comparison between a baseline balance batch and a candidate balance batch — the heart of AC1's comparison artifact — with deterministic, byte-stable output and no I/O or wall clock.

## Goal

- **As a game designer**, I want the `--tune` loop to produce a versioned before/after comparison of two balance batches (per-metric `DistributionStats` deltas plus per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas), so a single tuning edit is summarised in one auditable artifact.

## Expected behaviour

- New pure module `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` (or equivalent) that:
  1. Defines the versioned comparison types (per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas + per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas) with a schema version constant.
  2. Diffs two `BalanceAggregate`/`BalanceReport` pairs produced by the existing `runBatch` — reuse the shared `DistributionStats`/`BalanceAggregate` schema (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`) and `stableStringify` for byte-stable serialisation.
  3. Classifies each delta against a configurable relative ±10% mean/median threshold and flags distribution-shape changes (stdDev growth, median shifts) in the machine-readable output.
  4. Exports the comparison surface from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`.
- Pure only: no filesystem, no wall clock (same constraint as the epic). Same edit + same seeds must yield a byte-identical comparison artifact; a no-op edit yields zero deltas.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pure tune core computes a versioned before/after comparison of two balance batches with per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas (AC1 artifact) plus per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas.

- The comparison classifies deltas against a configurable relative ±10% mean/median default threshold and flags distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), echoing the same statistics in the machine-readable artifact (parent AC5).
- Pure comparison/aggregation logic and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock or I/O leaks into the pure core (parent AC6).

# Same-sweep guard: refuse cross-config comparisons

> **Headline:** Pure guard for the `--tune` loop (child of AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715): a baseline and candidate batch may only be compared when their sweep configuration is identical, with a side-effect check via the per-run record hashes. Covers parent AC2/AC3/AC6.

## Goal

- **As a game designer**, I want the `--tune` loop to refuse to compare two batches whose sweep configuration differs, and to error if an identical-config re-run drifts — so deltas are never computed across incompatible batches or corrupted by side effects.

## Expected behaviour

- Pure guard logic (in `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` or `src/ai/eval/engine.ts`) that:
  1. Compares the sweep configuration of both batches — `seeds`, `policies`, `ticks`, `dt`, `sampleEveryTicks` (already recorded in each `BalanceReport.config`).
  2. Refuses (error) on any differing field before deltas are computed.
  3. Errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs — reuses the existing per-run `recordsHash` (FNV-1a of stable-serialised records) to detect side effects; the reports' config blocks and hashes are the inputs that exist today.
- Pure only; the CLI shell surfaces the error message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tool refuses to compare batches whose sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) differs (parent AC2), before reporting deltas.
- The guard errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs, detecting side effects via the recorded per-run record hashes (parent AC2).
- Same edit + same seeds yields a byte-identical comparison artifact; the guard's identical-config check confirms determinism (parent AC3).
- Guard refusal and side-effect detection are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (parent AC6).

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` or `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — same-sweep guard
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` / `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — `BalanceReport.config` and per-run `recordsHash` inputs
- `src/ai/eval/tune.test.ts` — unit tests for refusal on each differing field and side-effect detection

# Declarative CSV edit with guaranteed restore

> **Headline:** `--set <file>.<field>=<value>` single-field CSV edit for the `--tune` loop (child of AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) with guaranteed byte-identical restore on success and failure paths, or an explicit opt-out to keep the edit. Covers parent AC4/AC6.

## Goal

- **As a producer**, I want one declarative edit applied to the real balance CSV and a guaranteed restore afterwards, so the checkout stays clean unless I opt in to keeping the edit.

## Expected behaviour

- New shell-adjacent helper (e.g. `src/util/csvEdit.ts`, pure string-level; the Node shell does the file read/write) that:
  1. Parses `--set <file>.<field>=<value>` and applies exactly one single-field edit to one of `enemy-configs.csv` / `ship-config.csv` / `difficulty-curves.csv` (header row identified by field name; quoted-field-safe).
  2. Records the previous and new value for the comparison record.
  3. Supports guaranteed restore of the byte-identical original on success **and** failure paths, with an explicit opt-out (`--keep-edit`) to leave the edit in place.
- Failure-path restore must be verified by test (e.g. simulate a mid-run failure).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A declarative `--set <file>.<field>=<value>` applies exactly one single-field CSV edit and records the prior and new value (parent AC1 edit step).
- After the run the edited CSV is byte-identical to its pre-run state on success and failure paths, or the user opted into keeping the edit; the working tree is clean otherwise (parent AC4).
- Restore-on-success, restore-on-failure and the keep-edit opt-out are covered by automated tests (parent AC4/AC6).

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — file read/write and restore orchestration (shell layer only)
- `src/util/csvEdit.test.ts` (new) — parsing, quoted fields, restore on success/failure, opt-out

# `--tune` CLI: baseline → edit → re-run → compare

> **Headline:** One-command loop on `scripts/evaluate.mjs` (child of AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715): `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set <file>.<field>=<value> ...` runs the baseline batch, applies the edit, re-runs the identical sweep and writes three artifacts plus a readable summary. Covers parent AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6.

## Goal

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run one `--tune` command that (baseline → edit → re-run → compare) reports exactly which balance metrics moved and by how much, so tuning is a fast, auditable loop.

## Expected behaviour

- Extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` (Q1-b: extend, not a peer script) with a `--tune` mode:
  1. Runs the baseline batch with the existing sweep flags (`--games`/`--seeds`, `--policies`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`) and captures the report.
  2. Applies one declarative `--set` edit (child: CSV edit + restore), then re-runs an identical sweep reading the edited CSV through the shared loaders (`hydrateBalanceConfig` / `loadBalanceConfig` — never a divergent copy).
  3. Enforces the same-sweep guard (child: guard) before comparing.
  4. Writes three artifacts under `--out`: `tune-baseline-report.json`, `tune-candidate-report.json` and a versioned `tune-comparison.json` (+ a readable `.txt` summary), and prints the readable summary to stdout.
  5. Restores the CSV on success and failure (or `--keep-edit`).
- `--threshold <pct>` configures the relative threshold (default ±10%). No production runtime impact; all logic stays in the dev/eval layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented `--tune` command runs the baseline batch, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs with an identical sweep and writes three artifacts: baseline report, candidate report and the versioned before/after comparison (parent AC1).
- The `--tune` mode chains to the same-sweep guard (refusing cross-config comparisons) and safe restore across success and failure paths (parent AC2/AC4), with no production runtime impact.
- The text output flags metrics that moved beyond a configurable threshold (relative ±10% mean/median default, `--threshold`) and notes distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), echoing the same statistics in the machine-readable artifact (parent AC5).
- The `--tune` flag parsing, orchestration and error paths are covered by shell and CLI-core tests; pure comparison and guard logic remain wall-clock/IO-free (parent AC6).

- `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` — comparison core + same-sweep guard (reused)

# Intake Brief — Increase the number of waves in the levels, add mini-bosses

**Work item:** AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (epic, high)
**Headline:** Grow the campaign to exactly 10 waves per level (100 waves over 10
levels), add a bespoke mini-boss as the 10th wave of every level, introduce 10
net-new alien archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon types spread
across the levels, and wrap it in a mini-boss reward loop (upgrade an owned
permanent weapon/power-up **or** unlock a new weapon type from a ~50%-locked
pool) plus a checkpoint save/resume at each mini-boss.

## Problem statement

The shipped campaign has only 2–4 waves per level (29 waves total across 10
levels) and a single final boss after Level 10 — there is no mid-level payoff,
no escalation hook within a level, and no way to resume a run. The operator
wants every level to feel substantial (10 waves), each level to end in a
bespoke mini-boss that grants a meaningful permanent reward, the campaign to
offer genuinely new content for the later levels, and the player to be able to
pick the run up again after closing the game instead of starting over.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want each of the 10 levels to take 10 waves and
  end in a mini-boss, so the campaign keeps escalating within every level."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want a mini-boss kill to let me choose between
  upgrading one of my permanent weapons/power-ups and unlocking a new weapon
  type, so my ship keeps growing in the direction I choose."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the game to save my progress at every
  mini-boss so I can close the game and resume from the last checkpoint
  instead of starting a new game."
- **Designer/content author** — "As a designer, I want 10 new alien archetypes,
  5 new power-ups and 5 new weapons spread across the 10 levels — alongside
  the existing roster — so the later levels introduce genuinely new content
  while every previous level's enemies can still appear."
- **Engineer** — "As an engineer, I want the new behaviour (mini-bosses,
  rewards, unlocks) to run through the shared core and be mirrored in the gym
  scenes, so gym↔game parity holds without divergent copies."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **10 waves per level, mini-boss as the 10th wave** — Every level 1–10 has
   exactly 10 waves; the 10th wave of each level is that level's mini-boss
   encounter (9 regular waves + mini-boss). The final boss still triggers
   after Level 10. Wave counts and progression are data-driven
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` / `LEVELS`) and verified by tests.
2. **Net-new content for later levels** — At least 10 net-new alien
   archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon types are added beyond
   today's catalogue (17 enemies / 11 power-ups / 11 weapons → ≥27 / ≥16 / ≥16),
   spread across the levels as appropriate, each exercised in a gym scene
   (gym↔game parity).
3. **Mini-boss reward** — Defeating each mini-boss grants exactly ONE choice:
   upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by one level, **or** unlock a
   new weapon type from the locked pool. ~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue
   is locked at Level 1 and becomes available through these mini-boss rewards.
   The choice is applied through the existing permanent-level machinery and
   choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`, `powerups/choice`).
4. **Checkpoint save/resume** — A checkpoint (level, wave, lives, score,
   minerals, permanent upgrade levels, unlocked weapons) is auto-saved to
   `localStorage` at each mini-boss; the main menu offers Continue/resume from
   the last checkpoint in addition to New Game; starting a new game clears it.
5. **Quality & documentation** — The full project test suite passes with the
   changes; campaign invariants (difficulty non-decreasing, level variety,
   archetype reuse) continue to hold with 10-wave levels; all related
   documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
   `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
   and the README.

## Constraints

- **Mini-boss is the 10th wave** (not an 11th phase) — 9 regular waves plus the
  mini-boss as wave 10 of each level (producer Q2).
- **Content is net-new** — the 10 aliens / 5 power-ups / 5 weapons are beyond
  the current catalogue, not counted against it (producer Q1).
- **One reward choice per mini-boss** (upgrade an owned item OR unlock a new
  weapon type); ~50% of weapon/power-up catalogue locked at Level 1
  (producer Q3).
- **Gym↔game parity** — gameplay changes must be mirrored in the gym scenes
  via the shared core; no divergent copies (AGENTS.md).
- Persistence follows the existing `localStorage` convention
  (`ai_hell_*` keys alongside settings/leaderboard).
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Risks, assumptions & failure modes

- **Scope creep (content volume)** — 10 wave rows × 10 levels plus 10 aliens + 5 power-ups + 5 weapons + 10 mini-boss designs is large. Mitigation: treat this as an epic decomposed under the plan skill; content is data-driven and additive, so per-item ACs can land incrementally. Record extra opportunities (e.g. more archetypes, boss-specific audio) as linked work items, not scope.
- **Difficulty-curve rebalancing** — widening levels to 10 waves each changes the non-decreasing difficulty curve and wave-gating invariants. Mitigation: extend `difficulty-curves.csv` monotonically and keep/re-run the campaign invariant tests (`campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`).
- **Balance** — 10-wave levels and mini-bosses lengthen runs; assumed acceptable (producer Q2), but difficulty tuning is expected during implementation. Assumption: wave-10 target difficulty sits above the level's regular waves but below the following level's opening.
- **Unlock pool definition** — "~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue" needs a concrete locked set. Assumption: the locked set is defined in data at implementation time, biased toward newly added and later-level items, and includes enough early options that a Level-1 player still sees choice.
- **Checkpoint scope** — saves permanent levels/unlocks and run state. Risk: checkpoint/continue interacting with telemetry, run-seed reproduction and leaderboard scoring. Mitigation: checkpoint stores the run seed and permanent progression; leaderboard entries from resumed runs remain valid via the existing serialisation path.
- **Save-compatibility** — a checkpoint written by an earlier build must not crash a later build. Mitigation: defensive parsing with safe defaults (same pattern as the `Leaderboard` corrupt-JSON fallback).
- Assumption: "all previous level enemy types can appear in higher levels" already holds via the sequencer and remains a constraint on the expanded levels (existing archetype-reuse invariant is kept).

## Existing state

- Levels: 10 already exist (`MAX_LEVEL = 10`, `BOSS_LEVEL = 11`); campaign is
  currently **29 waves** total (L1=2, L2=3, L3=3, L4=3, L5=2, L6=4, L7=4,
  L8=3, L9=3, L10=2), driven by `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` +
  hand-authored `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`.
- Enemies: 17 archetypes ship today (scout, diver, tank, phaser, swarm,
  asteroid, harvester + classic-arcade march, capturer, ghost-chase/ambush/
  flank/wander, grunt, raider, lane-traffic, orbital-strike). Levels 6–10
  already showcase the classic-arcade roster (AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2).
- Power-ups: 11 (shield, bomb, speed_boost, phase_shift, teleport, extra_life,
  magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, force_field, mystery_ufo). Weapons: 11
  (cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova,
  mortar, arc).
- A permanent/temporary level split exists (`powerUpLevels.ts`,
  AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP): hold-full rewards raise the
  permanent level for the run. A reusable choice overlay exists
  (`MineralChoiceScene` + `powerups/choice`).
- No mini-boss concept, no weapon/power-up unlock gating, and no run
  checkpoint/save (only settings, leaderboard and rules persist).

## Desired change

- Extend the campaign data to 10 waves per level (per-level mini-boss as wave
  10), keeping hand-authored `fixed`/`dynamic` mixing where it adds value.
- Add a per-level mini-boss wave/phase: WaveManager recognises the 10th wave
  of each level as a mini-boss encounter; PlayScene spawns the mini-boss,
  handles its defeat, and only then advances to the next level.
- Add 10 net-new alien archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon
  types, spread across the 10 levels (data + entities + spawners + gyms).
- Add the mini-boss reward: on mini-boss defeat, launch the choice overlay for
  exactly one choice (upgrade owned permanent item OR unlock a weapon type from
  the ~50%-locked pool); apply through existing permanent-level machinery.
- Add checkpoint save/resume: save at each mini-boss to `localStorage`;
  expose Continue from the main menu; clear on New Game.

## Key Files

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — extend to 10 rows per level; mark the
  10th wave as the mini-boss wave.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — `LEVELS` skeleton + per-level mini-boss wave
  entries.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — recognise mini-boss wave; boss-gating per level;
  progression to next level only on mini-boss defeat.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — spawn mini-boss at wave 10; launch reward choice;
  write checkpoints; resume path.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Continue/resume entry point.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` + new
  entity/spawner modules (`src/waves/`, `src/entities/`) — 10 net-new alien
  archetypes + 10 mini-boss designs.
- `src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` — 5 net-new power-ups /
  5 net-new weapon types (IDs, catalogue entries, level curves).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — permanent-level application for the
  upgrade path; unlock state for the locked pool.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — reuse the
  choice overlay for the mini-boss reward (already launcher-agnostic).
- New checkpoint store module (e.g. `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) + keys
  alongside `ai_hell_settings` / `ai_hell_leaderboard`.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — parity gyms for new aliens, weapons, power-ups and a
  mini-boss gym (pattern: `GymBoss.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — update wave tables, enemy/power-up/weapon catalogues, save-data
  section.

## Related work

- AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5 / AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0 — Game Design Document (10-level
  campaign, boss, power-up catalogues; save-data design §6.6).
- AH-0MU72ZK3P006CH9G — WaveManager wave/level progression (extension point).
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 — 5 new levels showcasing the classic-arcade roster
  (existing later-level content; the "net-new" bar is measured beyond it).
- AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP — permanent/temporary power-up and
  weapon level split (reward machinery basis).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice scene (`MineralChoiceScene`),
  reusable for the mini-boss reward.
- AH-0MUZMTSQF0054WI8 — dedicated boss-hit SFX cue (pattern for mini-boss
  audio).
- find-related report appended to this work item's description.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "At least 10 new aliens, 5 new power-ups, 5 new weapon types for the
  later levels" — measured against the current catalogue or net-new beyond it?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "net new — spread them across levels as you
  feel appropriate". Source: interactive reply on the work item. Research:
  current catalogue is 17 enemies / 11 power-ups / 11 weapons (verified in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/powerups/types.ts`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`); the classic-arcade roster (AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2) is
  existing content, not counted toward the net-new bar.
- Q2: Is the mini-boss the 10th wave or an encounter after 10 regular waves?
  One shared mini-boss scaled per level, or bespoke per-level designs?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "10th wave, 10 designs". Source: interactive
  reply. Interpretation: mini-boss **is** wave 10 of each level (9 regular
  waves + mini-boss), and there are 10 bespoke mini-boss designs, one per
  level.
- Q3: Reward + save model (reconcile the two reward sentences and the
  checkpoint requirement) — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "as recommended".
  Source: interactive reply. Recommended model (accepted): each mini-boss
  defeat grants ONE choice — upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by
  one level, OR unlock a new weapon type from the locked pool; ~50% of the
  weapon/power-up catalogue locked at Level 1, unlocked via mini-boss rewards;
  checkpoint auto-saved at each mini-boss (level, lives, score, minerals,
  permanent upgrade levels, unlocked weapons) to `localStorage`, with Continue/
  resume on the main menu.

# Provide upgrades more frequently (AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z)

## Problem statement

When the player's hold fills and they are offered a choice of power-ups and
weapons, items the player already owns (i.e. level-up offers) currently appear
only **10% more often** (1.1× weight) than unowned items. That bias is too weak:
players report/builds feel like they are constantly chasing new items instead of
steadily upgrading the build they already have. Owned items should appear
**25% more often** than unowned ones.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when the hold-full choice opens I want
  upgrades for items I already own to appear noticeably more often, so my build
  keeps improving rather than forcing me to collect new items."
- **Designer / balance owner:** "As a designer I want owned upgrades to be 25%
  more likely to appear so progression feels steady and an existing build is
  rewarded."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 25% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (`weapon-level` and
  `power-up-level`) receive a **1.25×** weight multiplier during candidate
  selection; unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0×. Interpreted as the natural
  extension of the existing convention: "10% more likely" = 1.1×, therefore
  "25% more likely" = 1.25× (multiplicative, not +25 percentage points).
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The new value is the named constant
  `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` in `src/powerups/choice.ts` — no magic numbers,
  and no copy of the weighting anywhere else.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** Behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every
  gym that opens the hold-full choice (they share `src/powerups/choice.ts` and
  `MineralChoiceScene`); the repo-wide duplicate-body/parity guards still pass.
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Tests updated so the full suite is green:
  (a) the constant asserts 1.25; (b) unit tests assert owned candidates weigh
  1.25× and unowned 1.0×; (c) the deterministic weighted-draw test and the
  10,000-trial distribution test are recalibrated to the 1.25 / 2.25 weighted
  probability (tolerance band ±3% retained); (d) the docs-guard test
  (`src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts`) reflects 1.25× / 25%.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  change: code comments in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `README.md` (§
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` description), and `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§4.5 hold-full choice and the architecture diagram line recording 1.1×),
  plus `docs/BALANCING.md` if it mentions the owned-upgrade weights.
- **AC6 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** the shared behaviour lives once in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` and is consumed by the game and every gym — this
  change only edits that shared module and its docs/tests.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy`
  interface or `ChoiceOption` shape; only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no persistence or leaderboard impact.
- **Wording transparency:** player-facing copy should continue to describe the
  items, not the odds — the 25% bias is a selection-policy detail, not UI copy.

## Existing state

`OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1` in `src/powerups/choice.ts` (added by
AH-0MUY47W62005FF74, shipped in v0.1.11). The weighted selection lives in
`drawWeightedWithoutReplacement` inside `createRandomChoiceStrategy`; owned
`weapon-level`/`power-up-level` offers get the 1.1× weight while unowned base
entries get 1.0×. Docs guard `src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts` pins 1.1× /
"10% more likely" in `README.md` and the GDD — any value change requires those
documents to move in lockstep or the guard fails.

## Desired change

- Change `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` from `1.1` to `1.25` in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts`, updating the doc comments ("10%" → "25%").
- Recalibrate unit tests (`src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`):
  constant assertion, weight assertions, the deterministic draw expectation
  (with total weight 2.25, r=0.48 → threshold 1.08 still crosses the 1.0
  unowned weight and lands on the owned level-up — verify the comment and
  thresholds hold), and the 10,000-trial ±3% distribution test against the
  theoretical 1.25 / 2.25 probability (still well within ±3%).
- Update the docs guard (`src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts`) and the documents
  it asserts: `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.5 + diagram
  row) from 1.1×/10% to 1.25×/25%.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` 1.1 → 1.25 and doc comments.
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — constant assertion, weight assertions, deterministic-draw test, 10,000-trial distribution test.
- `src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts` — docs guard pinned to the old 1.1×/10% values.
- `README.md` — § `src/powerups/choice.ts` description ("1.1×" / "10% more often").
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full choice and architecture-diagram row ("1.1×" / "10% more likely").

## Related work

- **AH-0MUY47W62005FF74 (completed)** — Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in
  hold-full choice. Direct antecedent: introduced `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`
  and the "X% more likely = (1 + X/100)×" convention; this item retunes the same
  knob from 10% to 25%.
- **AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2 (completed)** — Level-up offers duplicate weapon; the
  de-duplication in `buildChoiceCandidates` this weighting operates on.
- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR (completed)** — Show upgrade change summary and New
  badge in the hold-full choice list (display metadata; unaffected).
- **AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A (open)** — Extend the headless arena to simulate the
  full shipped campaign (find-related match); the retuned weighting is one of
  the tunables the headless arena would eventually cover.
- **AH-0MV55OC080068H03 (completed)** — Full-suite verification: typecheck,
  tests and build; this item reruns the full suite to confirm green.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "25% more likely" is a 1.25× **multiplicative** weight,
  consistent with the documented 1.1× interpretation of "10% more likely"
  (AH-0MUY47W62005FF74). If an additive interpretation (+25pp) were intended,
  the weight would instead be 1.667× — flagged for producer confirmation, but
  the multiplicative reading is the established convention.
- **Statistical tolerance (low):** the 10,000-trial ±3% test remains valid for
  1.25/2.25 (≈55.6% expected probability).
- **Docs-guard coupling (low):** forgetting to update README/GDD fails
  `src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts` — mechanically caught, not a silent risk.
- **Scope creep (low):** this item is a single-constant retune plus its
  docs/tests. Steering by player-input weighting (e.g. "favour the item the
  player picked least") is out of scope; record as a follow-up item if wanted.
- **Assumption:** "Hull full plugins" in the seed description is a
  transcription of "hold-full power-ups"; weapons items = owned weapon drops.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the seed description, the direct 10%
precedent (AH-0MUY47W62005FF74) and repo search fully determined the scope
(change `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` 1.1 → 1.25 and keep docs/tests in
lockstep). The one interpretive decision (multiplicative 1.25× vs additive) is
recorded above as an assumption following the established convention.

## Addendum — post-audit retune to 35% (2026-10-20)

**Audit rejection (2026-10-20T08:17:22Z, rgardler):** "Rejected by manual review. We
still aren't seeing enough upgrades of existing items. Lets increase this by another
10 points."

**Re-scoped acceptance criteria (supersedes the 1.25×/25% numbers above; the single
named constant and single-source-of-truth rules are unchanged):**

- **AC1' — 35% weighting.** `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` becomes **1.35** (owned
  `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` offers weight 1.35×, unowned base entries 1.0×).
  "Another 10 points" is read as **+10 percentage points on the 25% bias → 35%**,
  i.e. 1.35× multiplicative, consistent with the established convention that
  "X% more likely" = (1 + X/100)×. (A +10% *relative* bump would be 1.375×; not
  chosen — see Risks.) **Flagged for producer confirmation.**
- **AC2' — Single source of truth (unchanged).** The value lives only in the named
  constant `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` in `src/powerups/choice.ts`.
- **AC3' — Gym↔game parity (unchanged).** Behaviour is shared via
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` and `MineralChoiceScene`; parity/duplicate-body guards
  still pass.
- **AC4' — Testing/validation.** (a) constant asserts 1.35; (b) unit tests assert
  owned candidates weigh 1.35×, unowned 1.0×; (c) the deterministic weighted-draw
  test is recalibrated to total weight 2.35 (r = 0.48 → threshold 1.128 still
  crosses the 1.0 unowned weight and picks the owned level-up; the r = 0.4
  unowned case still holds) and the 10,000-trial test targets the 1.35 / 2.35
  (≈57.4%) probability with the ±3% band retained; (d) the docs guard
  (`src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts`) pins 1.35× / 35%.
- **AC5' — Documentation.** `src/powerups/choice.ts` doc comments, `README.md`
  (`src/powerups/choice.ts` section) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.5 and
  the architecture-diagram row) all move in lockstep to 1.35× / 35%.
- **AC6' — Full suite.** Full project test suite green (CI/CD pipeline tests out
  of scope).

**Additional risk (vs the 1.25× plan):** the "10 points" phrasing is ambiguous
(+10 percentage points = 1.35× vs +10% relative = 1.375×); the percentage-point
reading is assumed and recorded here for producer confirmation.

# Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool

Defeating a mini-boss grants exactly one choice — upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by one level, or unlock a new weapon type from a ~50%-locked pool — applied through the existing permanent-level machinery (epic AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On mini-boss defeat, exactly ONE choice is offered via the existing choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene` + `powerups/choice`), launcher-agnostic.

3. Option B unlocks one weapon type from a data-defined locked pool; ~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue is locked at Level 1 (invariant test).
4. Only one choice is consumed per mini-boss; the choice is applied for the run; unlocking persists to the checkpoint state.
5. Tests cover both options, the ~50% invariant, and single-choice consumption.

- Add unlock-state helper + locked-pool data (bias toward new/late items).
- PlayScene defeat → launch `MineralChoiceScene` with the upgrade-or-unlock option set; apply via `applyMineralChoiceReward`-style path.

# Snap enemy pitch automation to A natural minor (AC3)

**Parent:** Balance the levels of all enemy sounds (AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q)

Snap every pitched-oscillator automation point (start / end / waypoints) in every enemy recipe to the nearest A natural minor note (`A B C D E F G`, equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz). Convert multi-seed pitch-jitter ranges to scale-degree variants (each seed starts on a different A-minor note and descends to an A-minor note), preserving per-kill variation without off-scale pitches. Filtered-noise-only cues documented as unpitched / conformant-by-nature.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ] **AC3 — Scale conformance (A natural minor):** every pitched-oscillator automation point (start / end / waypoints) in every enemy recipe snaps to the nearest **A natural minor** note (`A B C D E F G`, equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz). Filtered-noise-only cues are documented as unpitched / conformant-by-nature. The multi-seed pitch-jitter ranges are re-derived as **scale-degree variants** (each seed starts on a different A-minor note and descends to an A-minor note), preserving per-kill variation without off-scale pitches.

- Every pitched automation frequency in every enemy recipe is an A natural minor note (≤ 1 Hz tolerance to nearest equal-tempered A-minor note)
- Multi-seed jitter ranges (enemy-destruction, diver-destruction, boss-phase-cue) converted to scale-degree variants: each seed anchored on a distinct A-minor note pair
- Per-kill variation preserved: re-render still yields distinguishable variants within each range
- Filtered-noise-only cues (if any) documented as unpitched / conformant-by-nature in the recipe docs and report
- Guard test (AC5 child) passes on scale assertions once re-rendered
- Existing in-scale frequencies (e.g. enemy-spawn 220→880 Hz) unchanged; off-scale ones (tank-fire 90→28 Hz, phaser-advance 660→880 Hz) snapped

- Updated `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` automation frequency values + scale-degree variant seeds

**Dependencies:** After amplitude tiers (shared recipe-edit surface, single re-render pass); scale snap may be combined with tier edits on the same recipes.

## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage

## Goal

Replace the arena's fixed two-to-N-wave hostile reservoir (skirmish model) with the **shared campaign sequencer**: the arena builds the shipped campaign via `buildSequencedLevels(rows, defaultCandidatePool, { seed })` (honouring `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), drives the shared `WaveManager` state machine, spawns from `planSpawns(seededRng)`, gates wave/level completion through `onEnemyDestroyed`, and emits the canonical `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry events so `waveReached` and `levelReached` become meaningful, non-zero distributions in batch reports.

## User story

As a game designer, I want a bot batch to play the same campaign the game ships (all levels/waves via the shared sequencer), so per-wave difficulty targets can be tuned from evidence instead of intuition.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** One arena run plays the shared campaign (all levels and waves of the shipped definition, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes) and emits real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` records with the canonical payloads from `runTelemetry.ts` (`level`, `waveNumber`, `waveCount`); a batch report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`.
- **AC2:** Wave/level progression is driven exclusively by the shared `WaveManager` (`beginGame`, `planSpawns`, `onEnemyDestroyed`) and `buildSequencedLevels` — no divergent copy of campaign, wave, enemy or ship stats in src/ai/eval/ (asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards).
- **AC3:** The `dynamic` wave mode derives from the run seed exactly as the game does (buildSequencedLevels `{ seed }`), so two runs with the same seed produce the same campaign for byte-identical telemetry.
- **AC4:** The Level-10 boss trigger is treated as the end of the run (no boss/mini-boss simulation this round — fidelity boundary, parent Q2=a); the boundary is documented in code.
- **AC5:** Determinism preserved: same seed + config + policy produces identical records on the campaign path; run never reads the wall clock.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover progression, canonical event emission, seed-derived dynamic mode, and the no-divergent-copy guard; they pass under Node/vitest headless.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — drive buildSequencedLevels + WaveManager; emit wave/level events
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — campaign progression, event payloads, dynamic-mode seed tests
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — shared state machine consumed by the arena
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — shared campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static LEVELS skeleton merged by the builder
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical wave_start/wave_cleared/level_cleared event names
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — telemetry/types consumed by metrics (verify/keep)

## Goal

Model the mineral hold and the hold-full upgrade-choice loop in the arena using the **shared choice system** (`chooseOptions`/`randomChoiceStrategy` from src/powerups/choice.ts with the run's seeded RNG), so the arena emits `hold_full` and canonical `choice_selected` events and report `upgradesSelected` becomes a meaningful per-choice-id distribution. The bot picks among the offered options using the same seeded stream (parent Q1=a). Choices permanently affect the run (ownership context carried into later choice offers) via the headless-safe adapter identified in the spike child.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want the arena to exercise the same upgrade-choice flow the game ships, so per-upgrade balance can be measured from bot runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A run collects minerals into a shared-model hold (`MineralHold` semantics: capacity, growth multiplier, overflow); when the hold fills, the arena offers options via shared `chooseOptions(3, randomChoiceStrategy, seededRng, context)` and emits `hold_full` with the offered option ids.
- **AC2:** The bot selects one offered option via the run's seeded RNG stream; the arena emits `choice_selected` with the canonical `{ index, id }` payload; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3:** The reward is applied through the shared reward path (or the named headless adapter from the spike) so later choice offers carry accurate owned-weapon/power-up context (weapon-level/power-up-level options) — no invented option model in src/ai/eval/.
- **AC4:** Deterministic per seed: the same seed yields the same choice offers and selections (byte-identical telemetry).
- **AC5:** Unit tests cover hold-full triggering, canonical event payloads, ownership-context carry-over, and seeded determinism; they pass headless under Node/vitest.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — mineral hold, choice offers, selection, choice_selected emission
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — hold-full, event payloads, ownership context, determinism tests
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared chooseOptions/randomChoiceStrategy/buildChoiceCandidates
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold semantics (capacity, growth, overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (headless adapter from spike)
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical hold_full/choice_selected event names
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — already parses choice_selected; verify/keep
- **AC6 (parent-AC2 traceability):** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On the frame `isPhased` rises, the treatment emits a brief ripple/burst (short sharp chromatic-split surge with a flicker step, ≈150–250 ms) that reads as a glitch hit and is visually distinct from player-death juice — no camera shake; the existing screen-wide dim + split overlays are retained.
- While `isPhased` stays true, the chromatic split is more vivid and pulsing: split alpha raised from 0.10 toward ~0.20, split offset raised from 3 px toward ~6 px with a slow oscillation, plus a subtle alpha flicker (≈2–4 Hz) and a soft colour-pulse between the two split hues.

# Tests: pure compile-promo edit-plan and selection (test-first)

## Goal

Author the hermetic test suite that defines the pure contract of
`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` **before** the implementation, so the edit-plan and
selection logic is specified and verifiable without ffmpeg or a browser.

**User story:** As a maintainer, the compiler's pure selection/planning logic
is covered by hermetic tests, so I can refactor the pipeline confidently and
the promo edit points are deterministic.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Test file and harness.** `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` exists and
  is picked up by the existing vitest include (`scripts/**/*.test.ts`). Tests
  use **synthetic series fixtures** only — no ffmpeg, no browser, no captured
  footage.
- **AC2 — Peak-window selection specified.** Tests assert the §7.5 recipe:
  peaks where `burstiness >= 0.15` **or** `intensity >= 0.7`, merged within a
  1.0 s gap, expanded by `lead = 1.5 s` / `tail = 1.0 s`, start clamped at 0,
  overlapping windows merged.
- **AC3 — Series→video mapping.** Tests assert `mapTimeToVideo` semantics
  (`videoTimeMs(t) = clamp0(t − (capture_started − run_startedAt))`) including
  the missing-anchor fall-back.
- **AC4 — Target-length sizing.** Tests assert the plan is sized to the
  reported targets: promo ~45–60 s, showreel > 2 min, and a set of short
  highlight clips — with deterministic segment selection when the pool
  exceeds or falls short of the target.
- **AC5 — Feature coverage & dedupe.** Tests assert the editorial config
  guarantees weapons, pickups and enemies are each represented (boss included
  when footage exists) and that repeated near-identical moments are deduped.
- **AC6 — Deterministic ordering.** Same inputs ⇒ byte-identical edit plan
  and manifests (stable ordering, no wall-clock/random dependence).
- **AC7 — Manifest shapes.** Tests assert the **selection manifest** (source
  WebM, `.action.jsonl`, mapped video timestamps, motivating intensity values)
  and the **coverage manifest** (feature → clip + timestamp ranges) shapes.
- **AC8 — Failing-first.** The tests fail against the absent implementation
  (red before green) and pass once this item's sibling implementation lands.

- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — new hermetic test suite
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — module under test (created by the sibling item)

- Follow the style of existing `scripts/*.test.ts` hermetic tests.

  single peak, all-peaks, gap exactly at threshold, short pool).

## Deliverables

- Hermetic, red-first test suite for the pure compile logic.

# Capture: export action-intensity series + join anchor

## Goal

Make `npm run capture` persist, next to each captured WebM, the per-run
action-intensity series and the §7.5 video-join anchor, so the promo compile
pipeline can select peaks automatically and offline.

**User story:** As the maintainer, when I run `npm run capture`, I get the
`.action.jsonl` series and join anchor alongside the WebM so the compiler can
map action-intensity peaks to video timestamps without re-running the game.

## Problem / discovery

The work item assumes per-run `.action.jsonl` records already exist, but a
repository investigation (this planning session, 2026-10-18) found **no
`.action.jsonl` files on disk in `capture-output/`** and **no production
caller of `serialiseActionIntensitySeries`** (only its test). Today:

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` writes only the WebM; telemetry
  (`state.actionIntensity`) lives in the page's JSONL telemetry sink
  (`localStorage` key `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`).
- The pure serialiser `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.ts` exists and
  is unit-tested, but is never invoked to write a file.
- The `capture_started` marker (`buildCaptureStartedMarker`, §7.5) is returned
  in the capture result object in memory but is not persisted.
- `run_startedAt` (telemetry run-header `startedAt`) is likewise not persisted
  next to the WebM.

This blocks AC2 of the parent: the compile pipeline has no automated peak
input. This item closes that gap using the **already-documented** convention
(`docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.3: `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`)
and reuses the existing pure serialiser (no new format invention).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Series written.** A completed capture writes
  `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`, basename matching the WebM
  (`gameplay-<timestamp>.webm` → `gameplay-<timestamp>.action.jsonl`), using
  the documented header (`schemaVersion`, `runSeed`, `sampleRateHz`,
  `categories`) and one sample line per recorded tick (`t`, `tick`,
  `rawScore`, `intensity`, `smoothed`, `burstiness`, `breakdown`).
- **AC2 — Join anchor persisted.** The §7.5 join inputs — the
  `capture_started` epoch-ms marker and the telemetry run-header
  `startedAt` epoch ms — are persisted alongside the WebM (sidecar or series
  header extension) so `mapTimeToVideo` can run offline and deterministically.
- **AC3 — No capture regression.** Capture output (resolution, codec, audio,
  non-black fraction) and existing capture tests are unchanged; the export is
  additive and tolerant of partial runs (header-only series is valid).
- **AC4 — Hermetic tests.** The pure export/naming/anchor logic is unit-tested
  hermetically (no browser, no ffmpeg); a test covers basename mapping, anchor
  serialisation, and truncated/partial series tolerance.
- **AC5 — Discoverable.** `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs --help` (and/or the
  run summary) documents the new outputs.

## Key files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — write the series + anchor after recording
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.d.mts` — declare new exports/result fields
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests for new pure logic
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.ts` — reuse (do not fork the format)
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.3/§7.5 — canonical convention

## Implementation notes

- Reuse the existing serialiser format verbatim; if the TS module is not
  importable from the `.mjs` script, port only the pure formatting into a
  small `.mjs` helper (repo convention) and keep the TS module as the schema
  reference.
- The page-side series can be read via `page.evaluate` from the telemetry
  sink / an exposed dev handle at run end.
- Prefer a sidecar (`<run-id>.capture.json`) for the anchor over changing the
  versioned series header; document whichever is chosen.

## Deliverables

- Capture emits `<run-id>.action.jsonl` + a join anchor for every run.
- Hermetic tests green.

## Dependencies

- None (prerequisite for the compile pipeline).
data.title: Capture: export action-intensity series + join anchor

# Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic in compile-promo

## Goal

Implement the pure, committed selection/planning logic of the promo compiler
(`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts`): read each
source run's `.action.jsonl`, compute highlight windows with the documented
§7.5 recipe, map to video time, and produce an ordered edit plan sized to the
three deliverable targets, emitting the **selection manifest** (AC2 of the
parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can run a committed script that turns my
captured runs' action-intensity series into an ordered edit plan, so the promo
is driven by measured on-screen action rather than hand-picked moments.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Series reader.** Parses `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`
  (header + one sample per line), skipping malformed/truncated lines and
  tolerating header-only files.
- **AC2 — Window selection.** Produces highlight windows matching the
  documented recipe (§7.5 thresholds `θ=0.15`, `I_hi=0.7`, `g=1.0 s`,
  `lead=1.5 s`, `tail=1.0 s`, merged + clamped) — consistent with
  `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts`.
- **AC3 — Video-time mapping.** Maps window series-times to video times using
  the persisted join anchor (capture_started / run startedAt), falling back to
  approximate mapping when the anchor is missing.
- **AC4 — Sized edit plan.** Produces an ordered edit plan sized to the three
  targets (promo ~45–60 s, showreel > 2 min, several highlight clips),
  respecting per-source duration constraints; deterministic (same inputs ⇒
  same plan).
- **AC5 — Selection manifest.** Emits the selection manifest listing, per
  selected segment: source WebM, source `.action.jsonl`, mapped video
  timestamps (in/out), and the intensity/burstiness values that motivated the
  pick.
- **AC6 — CLI contract.** `scripts/compile-promo.mjs --help` documents
  inputs, outputs and prerequisites (ffmpeg); missing source footage or series
  yields a clear, actionable error. The pure path runs **without ffmpeg**.
- **AC7 — Type declarations.** `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts` declares the
  module's public types/consts so the TS test suite type-checks (repo
  convention).
- **AC8 — Tests green.** The test-first suite (sibling item) passes.

- **Covers parent AC2:** **AC2 — Automated action-intensity peak selection.** The editing source pool and edit points are driven by the recorded per-run action-intensity series: peak windows (`burstiness ≥ 0.15` and/or `intensity ≥ 0.7`, merged within a 1.0 s gap, with lead/tail padding) as implemented by the existing pure helper (`src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts`) and the highlight recipe in `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5. Each selected segment is verifiable: a selection manifest lists source WebM, `.action.jsonl`, mapped video timestamps, and the intensity values that motivated the pick.

## Key files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — new pure select/plan module
- `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts` — new type declarations
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — hermetic tests (sibling item)
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` — recipe reference (port the
  pure logic; the TS helper is dev-gated / not Node-importable)

## Implementation notes

- Keep the pure logic dependency-free and side-effect-free so it imports from
  the test suite without a browser.
- Reuse the anchor format chosen in the capture-export item (C1).
- Editorial ordering/dedup/coverage config lives in the sibling *Editorial
  config* item; expose the hooks here.

## Deliverables

- Committed pure compiler module + types, selection manifest, `--help`,
  green hermetic tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the test-first tests item (C2); requires the series + anchor
  format produced by the capture-export item (C1).

## Goal

Implement the ffmpeg-driven part of the pipeline (AC1, AC5, AC6 of the
parent): trim, reorder, join and mux source clips **deterministically via

(decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

**User story:** As the maintainer, one command (`npm run compile:promo`)
turns my captured footage into the promo package, and the script tells me
loudly and clearly when ffmpeg or footage is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — ffmpeg invocation.** Trims each selected segment to its mapped in/out
  points, reorders, concatenates and muxes audio deterministically; sources are
  the WebM (VP9+Opus, or VP8 fallback) produced by `npm run capture`.
- **AC2 — Three deliverable types.** Produces (a) a single compiled promo WebM
  of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (> 2 min), (c) several short
  highlight clips — all WebM at the game's full native 960×540 resolution with
  the game's own SFX audio track.
- **AC3 — Output validation.** A validation step confirms each deliverable is
  decodable, has non-trivial non-black pixels, carries an audio track, and is
  at 960×540; validation failures are reported with actionable messages.
- **AC4 — Clear errors.** Missing ffmpeg or missing source footage yields a
  clear error with installation/runtime hints (ffmpeg install commands in
  `--help` and docs), not a stack trace.
- **AC5 — npm entry point.** `npm run compile:promo` drives the pipeline; the
  driver documents inputs, outputs and prerequisites via `--help`.
- **AC6 — Hermetic separation.** The ffmpeg-dependent path is isolated from
  the pure logic; the pure parts remain unit-tested without ffmpeg (see the
  sibling pure/test items). An optional integration smoke test is gated on
  ffmpeg presence and real or synthetic footage.

- **Covers parent AC5:** **AC5 — Reproducible, committed compile pipeline.** A committed editor script (e.g. `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + an `npm run compile:promo` script) drives the compilation **deterministically via ffmpeg** (installed on the host, per producer decision): trim, reorder, join and mux the source clips without hand-editing. The script (`--help`) documents inputs/outputs and prerequisites, fails with clear errors when ffmpeg or source footage is missing, and its pure parts (manifest/selection logic) are unit-tested hermetically.
- **Covers parent AC6:** **AC6 — Testing/validation.** The pure selection/planning logic of the compile script has hermetic unit tests; the delivered video files are validated (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio track present, correct resolution) by a validation step in the pipeline.

## Key files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — ffmpeg driver + validation step
- `package.json` — `compile:promo` script entry
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — extend hermetic tests; integration gated on ffmpeg

## Implementation notes

- Prefer `ffmpeg` filter/`-ss`/`-to` trimming + concat demuxer (or a re-encode
  concat pass if the container requires it — see the capture doc's MP4/VP9+Opus
  note); choose the deterministic option and document it.
- Keep the deliverables under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree; never
  commit video files.

## Deliverables

- Committed ffmpeg driver + validation, `npm run compile:promo`, clear error
  handling.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the pure edit-plan/selection logic (C3) and the editorial config
  (C4); consumes the series + anchor format from capture-export (C1).

# Unit tests for wormhole-to-formation transit movement

## Goal

As a developer I want unit tests for the shared spawn-animation helper that pin down the
wormhole-to-formation transit movement, so that the movement is defined before it is implemented
(TDD, test-first) and cannot silently regress.

Part of **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (Enemies should emerge from the wormhole). Extends the existing
spawn-animation helpers in `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`.

## Scope

Add unit tests to `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` (extend the existing
"wormholeSpawn — enemy growth animation" describe block or add a sibling describe) covering
positional transit:

- The spawn state records a destination position and the entity's starting (wormhole-origin)

# Implement wormhole transit movement, parity and docs

## Goal

As a player I expect enemies to emerge from the wormhole and traverse to their formation
positions, so that spawning feels cinematic and diegetic rather than popping into existence.

Part of **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (Enemies should emerge from the wormhole).

## Scope

Implement the transit movement in the shared spawn helpers and wire both scenes to use it, so the
same code runs in the game and every formation gym (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).

- Extend `SpawnState` in `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` with the spawn origin and destination
  positions; extend `startSpawnAnimation` to accept a destination (defaulting to no movement for
  callers that do not need it) and `updateSpawnAnimation` to interpolate the entity's position from
  the origin to the destination over the spawn window, reaching the destination no later than the
  end of the protection window.
- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` — instantiate the enemy at the wave's wormhole position
  (`spawns[0].x, spawns[0].y`) and set its destination to the configured formation position
  (`spawn.x, spawn.y`). Spawn positions and timing must otherwise be unchanged.
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation` — the same pattern: create each entity at the formation
  base (wormhole) position and set its destination to its formation slot position.
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2.7 to document the movement phase and its
  timing, and update the relevant Timeline/Implementation/Tests bullets.
- Preserve all existing `isSpawning` spawn-protection gates (bullets, body collision, shooting,
  mineral absorption) and the single-live `WormholeController` lifecycle.
- Verify the Diver's existing movement/animation pipeline is not disturbed during transit.
- Run the full project test suite and ensure it passes.

## Acceptance Criteria


- Each spawned enemy starts at the wormhole position and moves to its configured formation position over the spawn-protection window; the same movement behaviour is applied consistently to both PlayScene and all gym scenes that spawn enemies.
- The movement completes within the existing 3-second spawn-protection window so enemies are fully arrived before the wormhole closes and before they become collidable.
- Spawn protection is retained during transit while moving from the wormhole: player bullets pass through, no shooting, no body collision, no mineral absorption (the existing gates on isSpawning apply), and the same movement behaviour runs in PlayScene and every gym scene that spawns enemies.
- docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md §2.7 documents the movement phase and its timing.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

# Phasers spawn in a line then snap to a formation

## Problem statement

When a wave containing orbital Phasers spawns, each Phaser travels from the wave's wormhole to the **grid/line** slot produced by its formation offset (`baseX + col × spacingX`), then **snaps** onto its orbital ring position on the first formation tick. Because a Phaser's orbital phase is derived from `offset.col × (π/2)`, any group larger than four Phasers repeats phases every four members — so with a scaled group (the difficulty sequencer can produce `phaser × 12`) three Phasers stack at each of the four points and the group appears to contain only four entities. The wave is harder to read than intended and the arrival looks broken.

## Users

- **Primary — player:** "As a player I expect a group of Phasers to stream out of the wormhole and settle smoothly onto their final orbital positions, and I expect to see every Phaser in the group, so I can read the telegraphed radial pattern and plan my dodges."
- **Secondary — developer / gym user:** "As a developer I expect the same orbital geometry to drive both the spawn-transit destination and the per-frame orbit, so the gym and the game cannot diverge (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md)."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No line then snap** — For an orbital (`phaser`) wave group, every Phaser's wormhole-transit destination is its **live orbital slot**, not the grid/line slot. During the spawn window the Phaser interpolates from the wormhole to its orbital slot and, when the spawn window ends, `applyFormationPosition` places it on that same point with no visible position jump (post-spawn position delta ≤ 1 px).
- **Distinct, evenly distributed phases for any count** — For a group of `N` Phasers, all `N` orbital phases are distinct and evenly distributed across the full turn (`phase_i = i × 2π / N`, `i = 0…N−1`). For `N = 4` this reproduces the existing square (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°); for `N = 12` twelve distinct orbital slots are produced with no two Phasers coincident.
- **Single shared orbital geometry** — One shared pure helper computes the orbital slot and is consumed by both the entity's `applyFormationPosition` and the scene's transit-destination resolver. No duplicated orbital maths (the repo-wide duplicate-body guard passes).
- **Gym↔game parity** — The same behaviour runs in `PlayScene` and in every gym scene that spawns Phasers (`GymFodderEnemies`), verified by tests on both paths.
- **Spawn behaviour otherwise unchanged** — Transit timing is unchanged (completes inside the existing 3 s spawn-protection window), and the existing `isSpawning` gates still apply during transit (bullets pass through, no firing, no body collision, no mineral absorption). The single-live `WormholeController` lifecycle is unchanged.
- **Testing/validation** — New unit tests cover the pure orbital-geometry helper (phase distinctness for `N = 4`, `N = 5`, `N = 12`; slot positions), the Phaser entity's on-ring placement, and the scene-level transit destination (game and gym). A regression test asserts that a >4-member Phaser group produces no coincident slots.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§4.1 E4 Phaser, spawn/formation sections) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 note the count-based orbital phase distribution and the wormhole→orbital-slot transit.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not change the Phaser's firing pattern, tell/advance-cue behaviour, health, visuals, orbit radius (`PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS`), or orbit angular speed (`PHASER_ORBITAL_SPEED`).
- Do not change spawn timing or the 3 s spawn-protection window.
- Do not change other enemies' formation or spawn behaviour; the shared helper must keep a sensible default (4) so single-entity constructors and existing tests are unaffected.
- Gym↔game parity: shared behaviour lives once in the shared core/helpers and is consumed by both the game and the gyms (AGENTS.md).
- Keep the pure orbital-geometry helper free of Phaser runtime dependencies so it is unit-testable.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Phaser.ts`
  - `_computeOrbitalPhase(offset)` returns `(offset.row × 10 + offset.col) × PHASER_ORBITAL_PHASE_SPACING`, with `PHASER_ORBITAL_PHASE_SPACING = π/2` — only four distinct phases, so counts > 4 collide.
  - `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, _spacingX, _spacingY)` treats the formation base as the orbit centre and places the body at `(centre + PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS·cos θ, centre + PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS·sin θ)` with `θ = phase + _localPhase × PHASER_ORBITAL_SPEED`. Spacing is intentionally ignored.
- `src/utils/formations.ts` — `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets(count)` returns `{ row: 0, col: i }` for `i = 0…count−1` (a line when fed through `computeFormationPosition`). There is no shared orbital-slot helper.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy(spawn, origin)` starts the wormhole transit with a destination resolver that computes `baseX + offset.col × spacingX`, `baseY + offset.row × spacingY`. For orbital offsets this is a horizontal line, hence the snap when `applyFormationPosition` takes over.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation(offsets)` uses the same grid destination resolver (`formationBaseX + offset.col × spacingX`, …), with the same snap.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — `SpawnState`/`updateSpawnAnimation` already support a live per-frame destination (`destFn`), so the fix can resolve the orbital slot every frame without new transit machinery.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `planGroupSpawns` derives offsets from `groupDef.count` but `EnemySpawn` does **not** carry the group count, so the per-entity config never learns how many Phasers are in its group.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — the Phaser candidate scales `count` from `max(1, floor(4 × 0.1))` up to `min(200, ceil(4 × 3)) = 12`; `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` records generated waves such as `phaserx12`, confirming >4-member groups occur in the shipped campaign.

## Desired change

- Add a **shared, pure** orbital-geometry helper (in `src/utils/formations.ts` alongside `computeFormationPosition`) that, given an orbital offset/phase index and the group count, returns the phase fraction/angle, and given the base + count + radius + elapsed angle returns the world slot. Both the entity and the transit-destination resolver must call it (Q3 = generic fix).
- Thread the group count to the orbital geometry so `N` is known at construction and at spawn planning. Candidates: an optional count/phase field on `FormationOffset` (populated by `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets`), or an optional `formationCount` on `EnemySpawn` → `createEnemyFromConfig` → `PhaserConfig`. Default to 4 when absent.
- Change `PhaserEntity._computeOrbitalPhase` to distribute phases evenly using the group count, and expose an optional **formation-slot seam** (e.g. `formationSlot(baseX, baseY)`) that returns the entity's live orbital point.
- In `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` and `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation`, for entities exposing the orbital slot seam, resolve the transit destination to the **live orbital slot** (re-evaluated each frame via the existing `destFn`) instead of the grid line; leave every other enemy's destination unchanged.
- Update the docs and add the tests listed in the Acceptance Criteria.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/formations.ts` — New shared pure orbital-slot/phase helper; possibly extend `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets` to carry the group count while preserving its offset ordering.
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — Count-based phase distribution; `applyFormationPosition` uses the shared helper; expose the optional formation-slot seam.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `EnemySpawn` (optionally) carries the group count from `planGroupSpawns`.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Thread the group count into `PhaserConfig` (if that route is chosen).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy` orbital transit destination.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation` orbital transit destination.
- `src/entities/Phaser.test.ts` — on-ring placement + distinct phase coverage.
- `src/utils/formations.test.ts` — pure orbital-geometry helper tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — scene-level transit-destination and parity tests.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §4.1 E4 Phaser and the spawn/formation sections.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E4 Phaser orbital behaviour.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (open) — *Enemies should emerge from the wormhole*. Generic wormhole→formation transit; parent epic. **Partial overlap only**: it defines the transit mechanism generically, whereas this item fixes the orbital destination and the phase distribution for Phasers.
- **AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6** (open) — *Implement wormhole transit movement, parity and docs*, the epic's implementation child.
- **AH-0MVDW2N6Y009DUY5** (completed) — *Unit tests for wormhole-to-formation transit movement*.
- **AH-0MURBER4L00821RR** (completed) — wormhole VFX, 1 px growth and spawn-protection gates.
- **AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC** (completed) — wave-portal placement and formation anchoring.
- **AH-0MVDW3R7300979DC** (completed) — drop placement avoids the formation slots of mid-emergence enemies.
- **AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT** (completed) — per-level archetype repetition cap (why a Phaser group can still scale to twelve).
- AGENTS.md **Gym↔game parity** convention and the `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (Q1 = A):** A single ring with phases evenly distributed using the group's actual count. For `N = 4` this preserves the existing square; larger groups spread around the same 80 px ring.
- **Assumption (Q2 = A):** Phasers transit directly from the wormhole to their orbital slot (no line phase).
- **Assumption (Q3 = A):** The fix is generic in the shared orbital-formation path, with Phaser as the only current consumer.
- **Risk:** `applyFormationPosition` advances `_localPhase` during the spawn window, so the live orbital point moves while the Phaser transits. The destination must be resolved per frame (the existing `destFn` supports this) or a position pop will appear at the end of the window.
- **Risk:** Threading the group count to the E4 geometry touches the spawn-planning pipeline. Mitigation: default to 4 and make the new field optional so single-entity constructors and existing callers/tests are unchanged.
- **Risk:** Adding an optional field to `FormationOffset` can break strict `toEqual` assertions in `formations.test.ts`; update those tests deliberately (and prefer a route that keeps `FormationOffset` minimal if a lower-impact option exists).
- **Scope creep:** Do not add multi-ring orbits, particle trails, new VFX, or change the Phaser's firing/telegraph behaviour; record any such idea as a separate linked work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should phasers be arranged when the group has more than four members?** (options: A evenly distribute phases across the single ring using the group's actual count; B multiple concentric rings; C cap the group count at 4) — **Answer (producer):** A. Source: interactive reply, this intake session.
- **Q2 — What should the spawn behaviour be?** (options: A emerge from the wormhole and travel directly to the orbital slot, no line/snap; B keep the line spawn and ease into the orbit after the spawn window) — **Answer (producer):** A. Source: interactive reply, this intake session.
- **Q3 — Scope of the orbital-phase fix?** (options: A generic shared orbital-formation helper; B Phaser only) — **Answer (producer):** A. Source: interactive reply, this intake session.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `wl search "phaser formation"`, `"spawn formation"`, `"orbital phase"`, `"phasers overlap"` and reviewed the candidates. Closest was **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (*Enemies should emerge from the wormhole*): its ACs cover the generic wormhole→formation transit and do not address (a) the orbital destination for Phasers or (b) the phase-per-count collision. **No full duplicate found**; this item is scoped to the phaser-specific orbital defect and cross-referenced to the transit epic.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6** – Implement wormhole transit movement, parity and docs (open)
- **AH-0MUJKJ8OO007TBSS** – Single-formation wave groups can declare more enemies than they spawn (completed)
- **AH-0MUGCQ8MS000815U** – Remove fixed asteroid group from Formations.ts (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv2sgix5005pfjt, absent, absorption, acceptance, actual (+357 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv2sgix5005pfjt, absent, absorption, actual, add (+348 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0murber4l00821rr, 0mv2sgix5005pfjt, 0mv8br9y70079tkc, absent (+345 more)
